A local attacker who pre-plants a symlink at that path can redirect extracted archive contents to an attacker-chosen directory.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Ruflo is an agent meta-harness for Claude Code and Codex. Prior to 3.16.3, ruflo's default docker-compose deployment… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Ruflo, an agent meta-harness for Claude Code and Codex, before version 3.16.3. The default docker-compose deployment exposed the MCP bridge POST /mcp and POST /mcp/:group endpoints without authentication. An unauthenticated network attacker could invoke tools/call to terminal_execute, obtain a shell in the bridge container, read provider API keys, and poison AgentDB learning-store patterns.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Phantom: Arbitrary file write and decode-bomb DoS via unconfined MCP tool paths In Phantom 1.3.0 and earlier, the MCP tools accepted arbitrary absolute output paths when PHANTOM_OUTPUT_DIR was unset, the default. Any caller able to send tool calls, such as an AI agent, could write or overwrite files the process user can write, including shell startup files. Separately, the stem-separation and render paths decoded input audio without a size or duration cap, so a small compressed FLAC or OGG file could expand to multi-gigabyte PCM and exhaust memory.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Stanza is a Stanford NLP Python library for tokenization, sentence segmentation, NER, and parsing of many human… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Stanza, the Stanford NLP Python library, before version 1.12.2. Model loaders such as stanza.models.common.pretrain.Pretrain.load() call torch.load(..., weights_only=True) but fall back to torch.load(..., weights_only=False) when a pickle.UnpicklingError is raised. An attacker-controlled malicious.pt pretrain or model file can therefore execute arbitrary pickle code when a Stanza NLP pipeline loads it.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Serena: Unauthenticated Flask dashboard on fixed port enables DNS rebinding → memory poisoning → RCE Serena's built-in web dashboard exposes an unauthenticated Flask API on fixed TCP port 24282 (hardcoded as 0x5EDA in constants.py), with no authentication, no CSRF protection and no Host header validation. A DNS rebinding attack lets a malicious webpage write arbitrary content to the agent's persistent memory, which the agent later reads and acts on, reaching execute_shell_command, enabled by default through shell=True, for remote code execution. The source states that any user running Serena with the default configuration is affected, and the chain requires only that the victim visit a malicious webpage while Serena is running.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Composio SDK before 0.2.32-beta.283 contains a path validation bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to read and… VULNERABILITY_ID affects the Composio SDK before 0.2.32-beta.283. A missing assertSafeFileUploadPath check in the readFileFromDisk function within tool-file-uploads.ts lets attackers use prompt injection to manipulate file_uploadable parameters, pointing them at sensitive paths such as SSH private keys. The CLI then uploads those credential files to attacker-controlled storage.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Gradio before 6.20.0 contains an open redirect and server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Gradio before 6.20.0. Unvalidated HTTP/HTTPS URLs passed to the file_fetch() function in the /gradio_api/file= endpoint enable an open redirect and server-side request forgery. A crafted FileData response can target internal endpoints such as cloud metadata services to retrieve sensitive credentials, including EC2 IAM role credentials.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise before 3.1.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in Faiss and SimpleStore vector store implementations that… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Flowise before 3.1.0. The Faiss and SimpleStore vector store implementations accept unsanitized basePath parameters from authenticated users, a path traversal flaw (CWE-22). An attacker with a valid API token can write vector store data to arbitrary filesystem locations, which the source says could enable code execution or data exfiltration.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability was found in bentoml OpenLLM 0.6.30. This affects the function async_run_command of the file… A command injection flaw, tracked as VULNERABILITY_ID and CWE-77, was found in bentoml OpenLLM 0.6.30 in the async_run_command function of src/openllm/common.py. VULNERABILITY_ID: ha-mcp: Add-on settings and policy routes are reachable without authentication at the bare root path The ha-mcp Home Assistant add-on, version 7.6.0 and earlier, mounts its settings UI routes at the bare root of port 9583 in addition to the MCP secret path. These root routes perform no authentication, no Origin check and no CSRF check, so any client that can reach the port can read or change tool visibility, feature flags, backups and the add-on itself. With Tool Security Policies enabled, the approval-policy API is also exposed, which can disable the human-approval gate on gated tools. Docker and standalone installs are not affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: mem0 contains unauthenticated config API endpoints that expose LLM API keys in plaintext and allow server-side request… VULNERABILITY_ID affects mem0 and describes unauthenticated config API endpoints. An unauthenticated attacker can retrieve stored secrets such as OpenAI API keys in plaintext via GET /api/v1/config/, or trigger server-side request forgery by setting ollama_base_url to internal addresses such as cloud IMDS through PUT /api/v1/config/mem0/llm.

VULNERABILITY_ID: @better-auth/oauth-provider's OAuth authorization-code grant allows concurrent redemption when two token requests race the find-then-delete primitive VULNERABILITY_ID affects @better-auth/oauth-provider at versions >= 1.6.0 and < 1.6.11, the embedded plugin in better-auth >= 1.4.8-beta.7 and < 1.6.0, and the legacy oidc-provider and mcp plugins. The POST /oauth2/token authorization_code grant redeems single-use codes through a non-atomic find-then-delete sequence, so two concurrent requests with the same code can both pass verification and each mint access, refresh and id tokens, contrary to RFC 6749 section 4.1.2.

VULNERABILITY_ID: 9Router before 0.4.44 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the unauthenticated POST… 9Router before 0.4.44 has an OS command injection flaw in the unauthenticated POST /api/tunnel/tailscale-install endpoint, which the dashboard middleware matcher does not cover, so no authorization check applies. The sudoPassword field from the request body is written to the stdin of a 'sudo -S sh' child process; when sudo does not prompt for a password (the process runs as root, NOPASSWD is configured, or a recent sudo timestamp cache exists), sh executes the value as a shell command, letting a remote unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary OS commands. The Shadowserver Foundation first observed exploitation on 2026-07-04 (UTC).

VULNERABILITY_ID: ONNX has Null Pointer Dereference in Upsample Version Converter Adapter (Zero Inputs) VULNERABILITY_ID is a null pointer dereference in the Upsample 6→7 adapter of ONNX's version converter, `Upsample_6_7::adapt_upsample_6_7()` in `onnx/version_converter/adapters/upsample_6_7.h:31`. When `convert_version()` processes an Upsample node with zero inputs, the adapter reads `node->inputs()[0]` without checking the input count, causing a SIGSEGV crash on Release builds and an abort on Debug builds. Any application running `convert_version()` on untrusted models is affected, and a 107-byte proof of concept reproduces the crash on onnx 1.21.0 and 1.22.0.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langroid: Neo4jChatAgent executes LLM-generated Cypher without validation (prompt-to-Cypher injection; config-conditional RCE), mirroring the SQLChatAgent bug fixed in VULNERABILITY_ID Langroid's Neo4jChatAgent sends LLM-generated Cypher queries directly to the Neo4j driver through its read_query and write_query paths, with no validation, statement-type allowlist, or opt-out gate. Because prompt injection can influence the query text, an attacker can read or destroy graph data and, when APOC or dbms.security procedures are enabled, reach OS-command and filesystem access. The report says this is the same defect class as the SQLChatAgent issue fixed in version 0.63.0 (VULNERABILITY_ID), and that the fix did not extend to the neo4j module.

VULNERABILITY_ID: 9router has unauthenticated CRUD on /api/providers and Full API Key Leak via /api/usage/stats 9Router, in versions up to and including 0.4.41, exposes its Next.js dashboard API without authentication. The /api/providers endpoints let anyone list, read, create, modify and delete provider connections, while /api/usage/stats returns full plaintext API keys. The /api/usage/request-logs and /api/usage/request-details endpoints also expose other users' request history and full conversation contents, including system prompts and messages.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM is a high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs. Prior to 0.24.0, a frontend-legal… VULNERABILITY_ID affects vLLM before 0.24.0, an inference and serving engine for LLMs. A frontend-legal multi-request speculative decoding workload makes the rejection sampler emit a recovered token at the vocabulary size boundary, which becomes -1 and reaches the model's embedding and attention path, crashing the engine worker with a GPU device-side assertion. A remote client that can send requests through the public gRPC Generate and Abort endpoints can trigger this, aborting concurrent requests and causing a service-wide denial of service until the worker restarts.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Coder's AI Bridge Proxy skips TLS certificate verification in default configuration Coder's AI Bridge Proxy (`aibridgeproxyd`) set `InsecureSkipVerify: true` in the default transport of its goproxy server, so outbound HTTPS to the Coder access URL accepted any TLS certificate when no upstream proxy was configured. An on-path attacker could intercept Coder session tokens, BYOK provider API keys and full prompt and completion bodies, and the default transport also honored `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY`. The AI Bridge Proxy was introduced in v2.30.0, and the v2.29 ESR line is not affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Suspended Coder users retain access to AI Bridge LLM proxy endpoints Coder's AI Bridge authorization logic, implemented in `Server.IsAuthorized` in `coderd/aibridgedserver`, does not check whether a user account is suspended, so a suspended user's unexpired API key keeps working against AI Bridge LLM proxy endpoints. The flaw affects AI Bridge from v2.30.0 onward, and the v2.29 ESR line is not affected. An attacker holding such a token can consume paid provider resources billed to the deployment and, if injected MCP tools are enabled, invoke those tools until the token expires.

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: Coder vulnerable to denial of service via unbounded request body in AI Bridge provider endpoints Coder's AI Bridge provider handlers read request bodies with io.ReadAll and no maximum size, so an authenticated user with AI Bridge access can exhaust memory with an oversized or chunked body sent to endpoints such as /api/v2/aibridge/anthropic/v1/messages. Because AI Bridge runs in-process with coderd, the process crashes, taking down the API, workspace coordinator and DERP relay. The affected AI Bridge provider endpoints exist only on the v2.33 and v2.34 lines.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Coder's sub-agent app registration bypasses template port-sharing policy enforcement The `CreateSubAgent` RPC in Coder did not check a requested app sharing level against the template's `MaxPortSharingLevel` before saving workspace apps. A workspace owner with an agent token could register a sub-agent app as `PUBLIC` even when the maximum was `owner`, exposing it to unauthenticated users through the wildcard app domain. The issue affects only deployments using Enterprise port-sharing policy and wildcard app hostnames.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langroid: handle_message() executes user-supplied tool JSON without sender verification A Langroid application that exposes a chat interface to untrusted users can have registered tools invoked directly from raw JSON chat input, even when a tool is registered with use=False, handle=True. The tool dispatch path in agent_response() → handle_message() → get_tool_messages() does not check whether the message came from Entity.USER or Entity.LLM. Depending on which handled tools are enabled, impact can include file read/write, database query execution, or access to internal orchestration tools.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langroid: Sandbox Escape to Remote Code Execution via Incomplete `eval()` Mitigation in TableChatAgent Langroid's TableChatAgent and VectorStore evaluate LLM-generated tool messages with eval() when full_eval=True, passing an empty dictionary as locals. Because __builtins__ is not removed from the globals mapping, expressions such as __import__('os').system(...) execute, allowing a prompt-injected attacker to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on the host. The flaw is located in /langroid/agent/special/table_chat_agent.py around line 239 and /langroid/vector_store/base.py around line 225.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langroid: SQLChatAgent dangerous-function blocklist can be bypassed with quoted or schema-qualified pg_read_file calls Langroid's SQLChatAgent blocks dangerous PostgreSQL functions with a raw-text regex that requires the function name to be followed directly by an opening parenthesis. Quoted identifiers, inline comments, or schema qualification (for example pg_catalog."pg_read_file") pass the regex yet still execute pg_read_file on PostgreSQL, restoring the server-side file-read that VULNERABILITY_ID / VULNERABILITY_ID was meant to block.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. From 0.22.0 to 0.23.0, the /v1/audio/transcriptions… From vLLM 0.22.0 to 0.23.0, the /v1/audio/transcriptions and /v1/audio/translations routes call request.file.read() and fully load an uploaded audio file into memory before the VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB size limit (default 25 MB) is checked during speech-to-text preprocessing. An API caller who can reach these routes can submit an oversized multipart upload, causing memory allocation proportional to the file size before rejection, which can create memory pressure or terminate the process depending on deployment resource limits.

VULNERABILITY_ID: In Trail of Bits fickling versions up to and including 0.1.11, the UnsafeImportsML analysis pass unconditionally calls… In Trail of Bits fickling versions up to and including 0.1.11, the UnsafeImportsML pass calls AnalysisContext.shorten_code(node) on every import, which marks each import as already reported in the shared reported_shortened_code set. The MLAllowlist pass then receives already_reported=True for every import and skips its allowlist check, so standard library modules outside the UNSAFE_IMPORTS denylist can pass check_safety() as LIKELY_SAFE. Because fickling.load() passes that verdict to pickle.loads(), such a payload is deserialized and executed.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LangSmith SDK TracingMiddleware: Arbitrary server-side file read A flaw in the LangSmith SDK's TracingMiddleware lets an attacker who can send HTTP requests to a server running it make that server read an arbitrary local file and upload the contents to LangSmith as a trace attachment. Retrieving the contents requires read access to the destination LangSmith workspace, and triggering the read may not require authentication, depending on deployment. The flaw combines an unvalidated tracing-propagation header field (CWE-346), a type check that never engages (CWE-843), and a path traversal read (CWE-22).

VULNERABILITY_ID: SearXNG MCP Server: DNS-resolved Private Hostname SSRF in `web_url_read` The `web_url_read` tool in `mcp-searxng` is vulnerable to SSRF via DNS rebinding. The `assertUrlAllowed()` function in `src/url-reader.ts` checks only the hostname string against a private address blocklist and performs no DNS resolution, so a domain that resolves to a private or loopback IP bypasses the check. In default HTTP mode, where `requireAuth` is `false`, an attacker can read arbitrary internal HTTP services reachable from the server host without authentication.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SearXNG MCP Server: Unbounded Response Body Read Bypasses URL Size Limit in `web_url_read` The `web_url_read` tool in mcp-searxng enforces its 5 MiB response limit only by checking the `Content-Length` header from a preliminary HEAD request. When a server omits that header, `checkContentLength()` returns `null`, the guard evaluates to `false`, and `response.text()` reads the full body with no byte cap. An unauthenticated attacker who controls or can redirect to an HTTP endpoint can force unbounded memory and CPU use, causing a Denial of Service.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Network-AI: EnvironmentManager.restore() backup ID path traversal copies arbitrary directories into environment data Network-AI's EnvironmentManager.restore(env, backupId) builds the backup path from the caller-supplied backupId and checks only that the path exists, with no resolved containment check. A traversal ID such as../../../outside/source-dir copies files from an arbitrary directory into data/<env>, reachable by default through network-ai env backup restore --env <env> --backup <id>. Confirmed in Network-AI 5.12.1; no RCE chain was confirmed.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Network-AI: EnvironmentManager.backup() follows symlinked directories and copies files outside the environment root into backups Network-AI's EnvironmentManager.backup() recursively collects files with _collectBackupFiles(), which calls statSync() and therefore follows symlinks. A symlink under data/<env> pointing to a directory outside the environment root causes backup() to copy external files into data/<env>/.backups/<backupId>/, confirmed in version 5.12.1. The source reports no RCE chain.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Network-AI: ApprovalInbox HTTP server has no authentication — anyone can approve pending agent actions The ApprovalInbox HTTP server in network-ai (lib/approval-inbox.ts) has no authentication on any route and sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every route, including the state-changing POST /approvals/:id/approve and /deny. Any party able to reach the inbox port, including websites visited by the operator through wildcard CORS, can list pending approvals and approve them, which resolves the gate so the held high-risk action proceeds without consent. Affected versions are network-ai <= 5.11.0, and the flaw is mapped to CWE-862 and CWE-352.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Network-AI: AgentRuntime sandbox path-prefix checks allow file access outside the configured base directory Network-AI's `AgentRuntime` uses raw string `startsWith()` checks for sandbox containment, so a sibling directory sharing the `basePath` prefix (for example `/tmp/network-ai-sandbox_evil` against `/tmp/network-ai-sandbox`) passes the check. An agent or user able to call `AgentRuntime.readFile()` or `AgentRuntime.listDir()` can read or list files outside the sandbox, confirmed in version 5.12.1 with severity. Embedding applications that use `FileAccessor.write()` directly or auto-approve writes may also allow writes outside the sandbox.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Network-AI: Poisoned environment backup manifest allows arbitrary recursive deletion during backup pruning Network-AI's EnvironmentManager.listBackups() trusts the path field in each backup's _manifest.json, and pruneBackups() passes that path directly to rmSync with recursive and force set. An attacker who can write a manifest under data/<env>/.backups/<name>/ can make network-ai env backup prune, or any call to pruneBackups(), recursively delete an arbitrary path the Network-AI process user can access. The issue was confirmed in Network-AI 5.12.1, and the advisory notes no RCE chain was confirmed.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI: Arbitrary File Read/Write via `multiedit` Tool Without Path Validation The `multiedit` tool in PraisonAI (`src/praisonai/praisonai/tools/multiedit.py`) passes the `filepath` parameter directly to `open()` for reads and writes, with no path traversal check, workspace boundary validation, protected path guard or symlink resolution. VULNERABILITY_ID: LangChain4j: SQL injection via metadata filters in langchain4j-mariadb and langchain4j-pgvector The langchain4j-mariadb and langchain4j-pgvector embedding stores build metadata-filter SQL by concatenating filter keys, and in MariaDB string values, without adequate escaping. VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM: OOM Denial of Service via Audio Decompression Bomb vLLM's `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint limits the compressed upload size but not the decoded PCM output, so a 25MB OPUS file expands to about 14.9GB of float32 PCM at decode time, tested on v0.19.0. VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM: GGUF dequantize kernel int truncation exposes uninitialized GPU memory in multi-tenant serving vLLM's GGUF dequantize kernels in csrc/quantization/gguf/gguf_kernel.cu truncate tensor element counts because the to_cuda_ggml_t function pointer takes the count as a 32-bit int, while the caller passes m * n. The output tensors are allocated with torch::empty and left uninitialized, so when m * n exceeds INT_MAX the unfilled portion retains stale GPU memory. In multi-tenant serving this residual memory may contain other users' inference data, a silent confidentiality violation.

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: stable-diffusion.cpp is a pure C/C++ library for running diffusion model (Stable Diffusion, Flux, Wan, Qwen Image… VULNERABILITY_ID affects stable-diffusion.cpp releases before master-584-0a7ae07, a C/C++ library for diffusion model inference. The pickle.ckpt parser in src/model.cpp advances its buffer without checking remaining input, so a crafted or truncated checkpoint can trigger out-of-bounds reads. Exploitation requires an application or user to load a.ckpt file from an untrusted source, such as a model sharing site.
affected_vendors_raw: stable-diffusion.cpp; Stable Diffusion; Flux; Wan; Qwen Image; Z-Image; PyTorch

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n: Python sandbox escape An authenticated user with permission to create or modify workflows containing a Python Code Node could escape the sandbox and achieve arbitrary code execution on the task runner container. The issue affects only n8n instances where the Python Task Runner is enabled.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM: OpenAI auth bypass VULNERABILITY_ID is a vulnerability in vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API server that allows authentication bypass of the AuthenticationMiddleware. The flaw stems from starlette reconstructing the URL from an unfiltered Host header on ASGI servers such as uvicorn, letting an attacker control url.path and reach /v1 endpoints without the configured VLLM_API_KEY or --api-key. Instances behind an RFC-conforming web server such as nginx are not affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow: Unauthenticated Shareable Playground arbitrary local or S3 file read VULNERABILITY_ID describes an arbitrary file-read flaw in Langflow's Shareable Playground, also called Public Flows. Unauthenticated users can run a public flow through the /api/v1/build_public_tmp route, and its files field is read by Langflow and fed into the LLM. The file path can point to any path the storage supports, including a local file or an S3 path, depending on the flow configuration.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow: Unauthenticated RCE in Shareable Playgrounds Langflow's Shareable Playground, also called Public Flows in the code, contains a remote code execution flaw. The route /api/v1/build_public_tmp executes any public flow given its flow ID, and the data.nodes[X].data.node.template.code.value field accepts arbitrary Python code from the JSON payload. The source states the impact as unauthenticated RCE on any deployment with a shareable playground, and tested on commit 2d67402b1dbaefcbce85a244d4a6cd5e4bda1cfe.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow: Path Traversal in Knowledge Bases API via Creation Endpoint Langflow's Knowledge Bases API, specifically the POST /api/v1/knowledge_bases endpoint, builds filesystem paths directly from the user-supplied name field without sanitization or containment checks. An authenticated attacker can use traversal sequences or absolute paths to create directories and write embedding_metadata.json and schema.json anywhere the application has write permissions, enabling cross-user data compromise, arbitrary directory creation, and overwriting of existing knowledge base files.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM: Security Check Bypass via assert Statement in Activation Function Loading Allows Arbitrary Code Execution An assert-based security check in vLLM's activation function loading, at vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/activations.py:48, restricts which functions can be loaded from a HuggingFace model's config.json. When vLLM runs in Python optimized mode (python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1), Python strips the assert, so an attacker-published malicious model can pass an arbitrary function_name to resolve_obj_by_qualname() and execute code during model initialization. The attack requires the victim to load the malicious model and the model to use a cross-encoder architecture.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow: IDOR/BOLA in Monitor API — Missing Ownership Enforcement on 7 Endpoints Langflow's `/api/v1/monitor` router exposes seven endpoints that read, modify, rename or delete user-owned messages, sessions, build artifacts and LLM transaction logs without checking that the requester owns the target. Any authenticated user can act on another user's data by supplying a resource ID or `flow_id`, which is an IDOR/BOLA flaw. The source notes that `GET /monitor/messages` in the same file enforces ownership correctly, so the pattern existed but was applied inconsistently. The PoC was tested on Langflow v1.7.3.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LangChain: Path traversal and sandbox escape in LangChain file-search middleware and loaders Several LangChain components resolve filesystem paths or expand search patterns without confining the resolved path to the intended root directory. Affected behaviors include a file-search agent middleware that does not check glob patterns or symlink targets, configuration loaders that accept unconfined path fields, and path-prefix checks that lack a path-segment boundary. When these receive path values or search patterns influenced by untrusted input, including an LLM acting on untrusted input, files outside the intended boundary can be disclosed.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK): URL-Encoded Path Traversal in nltk.data.load() Allows Arbitrary Local File Read NLTK's nltk.data.load() and find() functions allow path traversal through the nltk: URL scheme, letting an attacker read arbitrary local files. The _UNSAFE_NO_PROTOCOL_RE regex check runs on the raw resource string before url2pathname() decodes %xx sequences, so encoded separators and dot segments such as %2fetc%2fpasswd bypass it. The issue is tracked as CWE-22 and affects NLTK 3.9.4 and earlier under the default ENFORCE=False configuration.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Nuxt: URL-handling weaknesses in `navigateTo` and `reloadNuxtApp`: SSR open redirect, client-side script execution via the `open` option, and protocol-relative bypass in `reloadNuxtApp` VULNERABILITY_ID describes three URL-handling weaknesses in Nuxt's `navigateTo` and `reloadNuxtApp` APIs. A path-normalisation bypass lets inputs such as `/..//evil.com` become protocol-relative redirects in SSR responses, and `navigateTo({ open })` and `reloadNuxtApp({ path })` can run script URLs or redirect cross-origin.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability was found in HKUDS AI-Trader up to 74caf996f78dcc0c657df8365c8544678a16e215. This affects an unknown… A vulnerability in HKUDS AI-Trader, up to commit 74caf996f78dcc0c657df8365c8544678a16e215, affects an unknown part of the file /api/research/agents.csv in the Research Export component. Manipulating it leads to information disclosure, and remote exploitation is possible. The exploit has been made public. The project uses a rolling release, so no affected version details are given.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Budibase: Unvalidated VectorDB Host Parameter Enables SSRF The VectorDB configuration endpoint in Budibase accepts a host parameter with no validation against internal IP ranges, reserved hostnames, or URL schemes, so any authenticated builder-level user can make the server open TCP connections to internal addresses or cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254. Timing and error differences let an attacker enumerate internal services, and retrieved cloud metadata could enable privilege escalation or lateral movement.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LangGraph has NoSQL parameter injection in MongoDBSaver, allowing cross-tenant state access LangGraph's `MongoDBSaver` in `@langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb` used `thread_id`, `checkpoint_ns` and `checkpoint_id` from `config.configurable` in MongoDB `find()` queries without strict type checks. Attacker-supplied operator objects such as `$gt` and `$ne` could be treated as query operators, letting them return checkpoints from other tenants, including state, metadata and pending writes.

VULNERABILITY_ID: IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.9.1 could allow an authenticated user to read or modify sensitive information by… VULNERABILITY_ID affects IBM Langflow OSS versions 1.0.0 through 1.9.1. An authenticated user can bypass authentication through insecure direct object references, allowing them to read or modify sensitive information. The weakness is classified as CWE-639, Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key.

VULNERABILITY_ID: IBM Langflow Desktop 1.0.0 through 1.9.2 IBM Langflow is vulnerable to server-side request forgery (SSRF). This may… IBM Langflow Desktop versions 1.0.0 through 1.9.2 are affected by VULNERABILITY_ID, a server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw classified as CWE-918. An authenticated attacker can send unauthorized requests from the system, which may allow network enumeration or facilitate other attacks. NVD has not yet provided an assessment, and the CVE was published 06/11/2026.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Claude Code Action: Malicious MCP Server Configuration in PRs Enables Remote Code Execution and Secret Exfiltration A flaw in claude-code-action combined checking out attacker-controlled PR head branches, reading `.mcp.json` from the working directory through default setting sources, and unconditionally enabling all project MCP servers via `enableAllProjectMcpServers`. An attacker who opens a PR containing a malicious `.mcp.json` can achieve arbitrary code execution on the GitHub Actions runner. This can expose workflow secrets such as API keys and tokens when a privileged user or automatic trigger runs the action on that PR.
affected_vendors_raw: Claude Code Action; Claude Code; claude-code-action

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: Anyquery has Path Traversal through `clear_plugin_cache`, Allowing Arbitrary Directory Deletion The `clear_plugin_cache(plugin)` SQL scalar function in `namespace/other_functions.go` in julien040/anyquery 0.4.4 passes the caller-supplied `plugin` argument to `path.Join` and then to `os.RemoveAll`, guarded only by an empty-string check. Because `path.Join` resolves `..` segments, a low-privileged bearer-token holder can send `SELECT clear_plugin_cache('../../../../tmp/target')` to the `/v1/query` HTTP endpoint and delete directories outside the plugin cache that the server process can reach. The report states a directory outside `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/anyquery/plugins/` was successfully deleted in a verified scenario.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM's Artifact Pin Decay allows pinned deployments to load unpinned code, weights, and processors VULNERABILITY_ID reports that vLLM's revision pinning does not consistently cover all artifacts loaded for a model. Deployments that set `--revision` or `--code-revision` can still load dynamic code, GGUF files, image processors, retrieval side weights, or same-repository subfolder weights and config from an unpinned or default revision, so the pin does not describe the full artifact set served. The source states this is not a `trust_remote_code=False` bypass, unauthenticated RCE, or a demonstrated artifact compromise. The strongest example is Kimi-Audio, whose `whisper-large-v3` subfolder loads outside the configured revision.
affected_vendors_raw: vLLM; Hugging Face; Kimi-Audio; Kimi-K2.5; Kimi-K2.5 image processor; BGE-M3; GGUF

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: LMDeploy is a toolkit for compressing, deploying, and serving large language models. In versions 0.12.3 and prior… VULNERABILITY_ID affects LMDeploy, a toolkit for compressing, deploying, and serving large language models, in versions 0.12.3 and prior. The source says a hardcoded "trust_remote_code=True" setting enables HF supply-chain RCE without user opt-in. As of publication, no publicly available patches exist.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('path traversal') in GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio Code… VULNERABILITY_ID is a path traversal flaw (CWE-22) in GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio Code. The source says it allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally. NIST has not yet provided an NVD assessment, and Microsoft Corporation is the listed source.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability has been found in yoanbernabeu grepai 0.35.0. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file… A vulnerability in yoanbernabeu grepai 0.35.0 affects the processing of indexer/chunker.go in its Qdrant Backend component, leading to use of a weak hash (CWE-328). The attack may be performed remotely, but the exploitability is assessed as difficult, and the exploit has been publicly disclosed.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Twig: Sandbox: multiple `__toString()` policy bypasses via unguarded string coercion points Twig's sandbox fails to enforce its policy for implicit __toString() calls in several constructs. A sandboxed template author can invoke __toString() on any object reachable in the render context, even when that class's __toString is not allowlisted. Confirmed bypass vectors include conditional expressions, the matches and loose comparison operators, Twig tests such as is empty, nested null-coalesce expressions, and the do tag and.. range operator.

VULNERABILITY_ID: praisonai-platform: Agent endpoints accept any agent_id without workspace ownership check, cross-workspace read/update/delete IDOR The agent CRUD endpoints in praisonai-platform (GET, PATCH and DELETE on /workspaces/{workspace_id}/agents/{agent_id}) check only that the caller belongs to the workspace in the URL. AgentService.get resolves agent_id by primary key with no workspace_id predicate, so a member of one workspace can read, modify or delete agents in another workspace by supplying that agent's UUID. The flaw is an Insecure Direct Object Reference, tracked as VULNERABILITY_ID.

VULNERABILITY_ID: MCP Server Kubernetes: kubectl-generic flag injection enables Kubernetes bearer token exfiltration The kubectl_generic tool in mcp-server-kubernetes passes user-supplied flags and args straight to kubectl with no allowlist. An attacker with limited access can plant a JSON log line that an AI agent follows, causing kubectl to send the operator's Authorization: Bearer token to an attacker endpoint via --server and --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true. The captured token can then be replayed against the real Kubernetes API server, granting the operator's service account RBAC permissions.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A weakness has been identified in thedotmack claude-mem up to 11.0.1. The affected element is the function… VULNERABILITY_ID affects thedotmack claude-mem up to 11.0.1. The function computeObservationContentHash in src/services/sqlite/observations/store.ts, part of the Observation Content Hash Handler component, uses a weak hash. Exploitation requires local access, has high complexity, and is described as difficult.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability has been found in onnx onnx-mlir up to 0.5.0.0. Affected by this issue is the function… VULNERABILITY_ID affects onnx onnx-mlir up to 0.5.0.0. The weakness is in the generate_hash_key function in src/Runtime/python/torch_onnxmlir/src/torch_onnxmlir/backend.py, part of the Placeholder Node Cache Handler component, which uses a weak hash. Exploitation requires local access, has high complexity, and is known to be difficult.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Improper neutralization of special elements in output used by a downstream component ('injection') in Copilot Chat… VULNERABILITY_ID is an improper neutralization of special elements in output used by a downstream component ('injection') in Copilot Chat (Microsoft Edge), classified as CWE-74. The source states that it allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. The NVD assessment has not yet been provided.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Microsoft Copilot allows an… VULNERABILITY_ID is a command injection flaw (CWE-77) in Microsoft Copilot, classified as Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command. The source says an authorized attacker can execute code over a network. NVD has not yet provided an assessment, and the record was published and last modified on 06/04/2026.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in M365 Copilot allows an… VULNERABILITY_ID is an improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') flaw, classified as CWE-77, in M365 Copilot. The source states that an unauthorized attacker can disclose information over a network. The record was published and last modified on 06/04/2026, with the CVE attributed to Microsoft Corporation and no NVD assessment yet provided.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability has been found in milvus-io milvus up to 2.6.13. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file… VULNERABILITY_ID affects milvus-io milvus up to 2.6.13, specifically the Grantee ID Hash Handler component in internal/metastore/kv/rootcoord/kv_catalog.go. A manipulation leads to use of a weak hash. The attack must be performed locally, its complexity is high, and exploitability is considered difficult, but the exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be used.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability has been found in Streamlit up to 1.53.0. Impacted is an unknown function in the library… A vulnerability in Streamlit up to 1.53.0 affects an unknown function in lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py, part of the Palette Handler component, and leads to use of a weak hash. Exploitation requires local access and a high level of complexity, and the source considers it difficult. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be used, and a pull request to fix it awaits acceptance.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A flaw has been found in MLflow up to 3.10.0. This issue affects the function mlflow.data.digest_utils of the file… A flaw in MLflow up to 3.10.0 affects the function mlflow.data.digest_utils in mlflow/data/digest_utils.py, within the Dataset Digest Computation component. The flaw causes the use of a weak hash and can be exploited locally, with high complexity and difficult exploitability. A published exploit exists, and the project was informed early through a pull request but has not yet responded.

VULNERABILITY_ID: huggingface/transformers: Arbitrary Code Execution During Model Initialization in the LightGlue Model Loading Path A flaw in the LightGlue model loading path of huggingface/transformers 5.2.0 lets an attacker-controlled model repository run arbitrary code during model initialization. The `trust_remote_code` value, meant to block remote code, is overridden by the `trust_remote_code` setting read from the untrusted `config.json` and passed into nested `AutoConfig.from_pretrained()` calls. Code runs even when the victim calls `AutoModel.from_pretrained()` with `trust_remote_code=False`. Affected deployment contexts include inference servers, notebooks, CI/CD pipelines and evaluation workers, citing possible credential theft, lateral movement and persistence.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. In versions up to and including 0.8.3… In LibreChat versions up to and including 0.8.3, users with only VIEW access to an MCP server can retrieve the server's decrypted admin-managed secrets through GET /api/mcp/servers and GET /api/mcp/servers/:serverName. The returned config includes plaintext apiKey.key and oauth.client_secret values, letting viewers of a shared MCP server exfiltrate the underlying provider credentials.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. In versions up to and including 0.8.3, the… LibreChat versions up to and including 0.8.3 resolve ${VAR} placeholders against the server's process.env during Zod schema validation of user-supplied MCP server URLs. An authenticated user can submit an MCP server configuration pointing to an attacker-controlled domain, causing the server to transmit secrets such as CREDS_KEY, CREDS_IV, JWT_SECRET and MONGO_URI in the request URL, without administrative privileges.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. In versions up to and including 0.7.6, an… VULNERABILITY_ID affects LibreChat in versions up to and including 0.7.6. An Insecure Direct Object Reference flaw in the PUT /api/keys endpoint lets any authenticated user add a userId parameter to the request body, which overwrites another user's API keys (such as OpenAI, Anthropic or Azure). An attacker could route a victim's conversations through attacker-controlled keys or cause denial of service with invalid keys.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenMed before 1.5.2 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the PII privacy-filter model loading path. The… VULNERABILITY_ID affects OpenMed before 1.5.2, where the PII privacy-filter model loading path contains a remote code execution flaw. The privacy-filter dispatcher applied broad substring matching to the user-supplied model_name parameter, so a value such as attacker/foo-privacy-filter-bar routed to a path that loads Hugging Face models with trust_remote_code=True. An unauthenticated attacker who supplies a malicious model repository with custom code referenced through auto_map in config.json or tokenizer_config.json gets that code imported and executed with the privileges of the OpenMed service process.
affected_vendors_raw: OpenMed; Hugging Face; PII privacy-filter model

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: F5-TTS through version 1.1.20 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the finetune Gradio handlers that allows… F5-TTS through version 1.1.20 has a path traversal flaw (VULNERABILITY_ID) in its finetune Gradio handlers. User-supplied project names are passed unsanitized to os.path.join(), so unauthenticated attackers can write arbitrary files, including via absolute paths such as /tmp/EVIL that override the base directory, anywhere the server process can write.

VULNERABILITY_ID: An issue in ESA AnomalyMatch before 1.3.1 allow attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted model checkpoint files… VULNERABILITY_ID affects ESA AnomalyMatch before 1.3.1. Its components load model files from session directories using torch.load() with unrestricted deserialization, so attackers can execute arbitrary code through crafted model checkpoint files. The weakness is classified as CWE-502, Deserialization of Untrusted Data.

VULNERABILITY_ID: praisonai-platform: Any workspace member can rewrite workspace name, description, and settings via PATCH /workspaces/{id} The praisonai-platform PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id} endpoint in workspaces.py is guarded by require_workspace_member, which defaults to min_role="member". Any workspace member can therefore overwrite the workspace's name, description and free-form settings JSON through WorkspaceService.update(), without an owner-role check. Because the settings object is read by downstream code, an attacker could alter configuration such as provider URLs or invite behaviour.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A weakness has been identified in zhayujie chatgpt-on-wechat up to 2.0.8. This issue affects the function… A weakness in zhayujie chatgpt-on-wechat up to 2.0.8 lets a remote attacker run OS command injection through the _get_safety_warning function in agent/tools/bash/bash.py, part of the Bash Tool component. A public exploit is available and could be used in attacks.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI has an Arbitrary File Write in Python API PraisonAI versions up to and including 4.6.37 skip path validation in `write_file` (`code/tools/write_file.py:77-83`) when `workspace=None`. Hidden metadata on a crawled webpage can then cause an agent to call `write_file` autonomously and write attacker-chosen content to an arbitrary path.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI's unauthenticated A2A official example can reach real LLM-driven `eval()` tool execution The first-party PraisonAI A2A server example combines three behaviors into a remotely exploitable chain: it exposes an A2A server without `auth_token`, binds to `0.0.0.0`, and registers a `calculate(expression)` tool implemented with Python `eval(expression)`. An unauthenticated client can send a JSON-RPC `message/send` request to `/a2a`, which passes the message to `agent.chat()`, and with a real Gemini model the LLM invoked `calculate`, executing Python in the server process. The advisory says the chain is confirmed for the official example and deployments following the same pattern, and that the full chain is only claimed for versions where the `/a2a` endpoint is present and confirmed.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI vulnerable to unauthenticated arbitrary file read via MCP workflow.show, workflow.validate, deploy.validate The fix for VULNERABILITY_ID / VULNERABILITY_ID is incomplete. Commit 68cc9427 added _resolve_rule_path() to rules.create, rules.show and rules.delete in mcp_server/adapters/cli_tools.py, but praisonai.workflow.show, praisonai.workflow.validate and praisonai.deploy.validate remain unchanged. A single unauthenticated MCP tools/call to praisonai.workflow.show can return any file the host user can read, and the dispatcher in server.py, which passes unvalidated arguments as **kwargs, is also unchanged.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI vulnerable to sandbox escape via `print.__self__` builtins module leak in `execute_code` (subprocess mode) PraisonAI's `execute_code()` in `praisonaiagents/tools/python_tools.py` (v1.6.37, subprocess sandbox mode) can be fully bypassed. Using `print.__self__` to reach the real `builtins` module, then `vars()` and runtime string construction to obtain `__import__`, lets an attacker run arbitrary OS commands on the host, defeating the sandbox. The bypass survives patches for VULNERABILITY_ID, VULNERABILITY_ID and VULNERABILITY_ID,

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI CLI automatically resolves @url mentions in prompt text and can read loopback URLs into model context PraisonAI's direct-prompt CLI automatically expands `@url:` mentions in raw prompt text before agent execution. The `@url:` handler calls `urllib.request.urlopen()` on the given URL with no loopback or private-address restriction and no approval gate, and prepends the response body to the model prompt, so attacker-influenced prompt text can pull localhost-only HTTP resources into model context.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI `deploy --type api` emits a Flask server with authentication disabled by default PraisonAI 4.6.33, the current @latest PyPI wheel, ships a code generator (praisonai.deploy.api.generate_api_server_code) that emits a Flask API server with auth_enabled defaulting to False in praisonai/deploy/models.py. The documented command praisonai deploy --type api therefore produces a server bound to 0.0.0.0 that exposes /chat and /agents without authentication, letting unauthenticated callers run praisonai.run() on user-supplied JSON. The record cross-references VULNERABILITY_ID (VULNERABILITY_ID) as a related issue.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI: Arbitrary code execution via unguarded `spec.loader.exec_module` in `agents_generator.py` - sibling of VULNERABILITY_ID PraisonAI's v4.6.32 refactor, which patched VULNERABILITY_ID / VULNERABILITY_ID by adding the PRAISONAI_ALLOW_LOCAL_TOOLS gate to tool_override.py, missed two spec.loader.exec_module call sites in praisonai/agents_generator.py. The functions load_tools_from_module and load_tools_from_module_class pass a module_path from YAML configuration to exec_module with no gate, no allowlist and no validation, and the source says this remains unguarded on master (v4.6.37). A module_path set through a recipe fetched via POST /v1/recipes/run can therefore lead to arbitrary code execution during tool registry construction, before any LLM call.

VULNERABILITY_ID: ouroboros-ai Vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via Untrusted Project-Directory.env Ouroboros loaded the `.env` file from the current working directory, so execution-affecting variables such as `OUROBOROS_CLI_PATH` and `OPENCODE_CLI_PATH` could be set by a malicious cloned repository. Running an Ouroboros command such as `ouroboros init` in that directory could execute an attacker's script instead of the intended CLI, leading to arbitrary code execution. The flaw is patched in version 0.39.0 via PR #1078.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastGPT is an AI Agent building platform. Prior to 4.15.0-beta1, the JavaScript sandbox worker at… VULNERABILITY_ID affects FastGPT, an AI Agent building platform, before 4.15.0-beta1. The JavaScript sandbox worker at projects/code-sandbox/src/pool/worker.ts:356 blocks dynamic import() with the regex /\bimport\s*\(/.test(code), which misses a block comment placed between import and (, such as import/**/("child_process"). Because import() is not wrapped by the safeRequire Proxy, which only proxies require, an attacker can load child_process and call execSync to run arbitrary commands as uid=100(sandbox) inside the sandbox container.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastGPT is an AI Agent building platform. Prior to 4.15.0-beta1, a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability… VULNERABILITY_ID is a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) flaw in FastGPT, an AI Agent building platform, prior to 4.15.0-beta1. An authenticated attacker can bypass the global isInternalAddress network protection and make arbitrary HTTP GET requests to internal network services. The flaw is reached through an incomplete fix in the dataset preview endpoint /api/core/dataset/file/getPreviewChunks when the externalFile data import type is used.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Koel Vulnerable to SSRF via Podcast Episode Enclosure URLs Koel validates podcast feed URLs with the SafeUrl rule, but episode enclosure URLs parsed from RSS XML are stored in the database without SSRF checks. When an episode plays, the server downloads the full response from that unvalidated URL through Http::sink()->get() and streams it back to the user, enabling full-read SSRF against internal services such as cloud metadata endpoints.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface that allows users to interact with text generation large language… SillyTavern versions prior to 1.18.0 expose the /api/search/searxng endpoint, which uses an attacker-controlled baseUrl directly to build outbound server-side fetches. An authenticated low-privilege user can point baseUrl at an internal or loopback HTTP service and receive the /search response body.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface that allows users to interact with text generation large language… VULNERABILITY_ID affects SillyTavern, a locally installed user interface for text generation large language models, image generation engines, and text-to-speech voice models, prior to 1.18.0. The POST /api/extensions/delete endpoint accepts extensionName: ".", which bypasses sanitize-filename validation and causes the entire user extensions directory to be recursively deleted. No authentication is required in the default configuration.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface that allows users to interact with text generation large language… SillyTavern versions before 1.18.0 accept the Remote-User (Authelia) and X-Authentik-Username (Authentik) HTTP headers to log users in when SSO is configured, without checking that the headers come from a trusted reverse proxy. Any network client that can reach the SillyTavern port directly can send these headers and authenticate as any user, including administrators, without a password. The flaw is exploitable only when sso.autheliaAuth: true or sso.authentikAuth: true is set in config.yaml, both of which default to false.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface that allows users to interact with text generation large language… SillyTavern versions prior to 1.18.0 use cookie-based sessions that store user handle and permissions in a signed client cookie. The endpoints POST /api/users/change-password and POST /api/users/recover-step2 update the password hash but do not expire existing sessions, and because the session is stateless there is no server-side way to revoke an issued token.

VULNERABILITY_ID: RAGFlow is an open-source RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) engine. An authenticated builder user can therefore make the server request internal addresses such as 169.254.169.254, which may expose cloud metadata credentials and internal services.

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: Microsoft APM is an open-source, community-driven dependency manager for AI agents. Prior to 0.13.0, Microsoft APM… Microsoft APM, an open-source dependency manager for AI agents, is affected by VULNERABILITY_ID in versions prior to 0.13.0. On supported Python 3.10 and 3.11 runtimes on Windows, the legacy-bundle probe used by apm install <bundle> calls raw tar.extractall() on untrusted tar members without rejecting Windows absolute member names such as D:/.... The flaw is reached when a local.tar.gz that is not a plugin-format bundle is passed to apm install.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Microsoft APM is an open-source, community-driven dependency manager for AI agents. From 0.5.4 to 0.12.4, two primitive… From 0.5.4 to 0.12.4, two primitive integrators in apm-cli enumerate package files with Path.glob() and Path.rglob() and read matches with Path.read_text(), following symbolic links transparently. A symlink committed inside a remote APM dependency under.apm/prompts/ or.apm/agents/ is preserved into apm_modules/ on clone, then dereferenced during integration, and the resolved content is written as a regular file into the project's deploy directories. The package content_hash, the pre-deploy SecurityGate scan, and apm audit do not flag this.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Microsoft APM is an open-source, community-driven dependency manager for AI agents. Prior to 0.8.12, Microsoft APM… Microsoft APM, an open-source dependency manager for AI agents, is affected prior to 0.8.12. When it normalizes marketplace plugins, it copies components referenced in plugin.json into.apm/ without checking that the attacker-controlled agents, skills, commands, and hooks paths stay inside the plugin directory. A malicious plugin can use absolute or../ traversal paths to copy arbitrary readable files or directories from the installer's machine during apm install.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Pipecat: Path Traversal in Pipecat Runner `/files` Endpoint — Arbitrary File Read via `%2F`-Encoded Separator Pipecat's development runner, started with the --folder flag, exposes a GET /files/{filename:path} endpoint in src/pipecat/runner/run.py that joins the filename directly onto args.folder without a containment check. Starlette decodes %2F after routing, so a request such as..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd escapes the folder, and the endpoint has no authentication. The advisory confirms this on pipecat-ai 1.1.0 and commit f078df78058ae82a02ce5b23e9e3a99a0917a53d.

VULNERABILITY_ID: python-utcp: Full Process Environment Exposed to CLI Subprocess - Secrets Leakage via Command Injection python-utcp's `_prepare_environment()` in `cli_communication_protocol.py` passes a full copy of `os.environ` to every CLI subprocess. Combined with the Command Injection flaw in `_substitute_utcp_args()` (VULNERABILITY_ID), an attacker can exfiltrate all process-level secrets, including cloud credentials, database strings and LLM API keys, in a single tool call. The issue is fixed in `utcp-cli` 1.1.2, which adds a `CliCallTemplate.inherit_env_vars` field to control inheritance.

VULNERABILITY_ID: @utcp/http: SSRF via attacker-controlled OpenAPI servers[0].url in HTTP communication protocol The @utcp/http npm package, versions 1.1.1 and earlier, contains a blind SSRF flaw in its manual discovery and tool invocation paths. The registerManual() check against an HTTPS/loopback allowlist is not reapplied in callTool(), and the OpenApiConverter trusts servers[0].url from an attacker-hosted OpenAPI spec, so an attacker can point generated tools at internal addresses such as http://169.254.169.254 or http://127.0.0.1:9090. The earlier startsWith('http://localhost') guard also let http://localhost.evil.com through.

VULNERABILITY_ID: DeepSeek TUI: task_create Insecure Defaults Enable RCE via Prompt Injection in Project Files The task_create tool in DeepSeek TUI spawns durable sub-agents that default to allow_shell=true (config.rs:1499) and auto_approve=true (task_manager.rs:297). A user who approves a benign-looking task_create call therefore unknowingly grants the sub-agent unapproved shell access, which can follow attacker-controlled instructions in a cloned repository's AGENTS.md file and run commands without a further approval prompt. The reporter demonstrates remote code execution through a proof of concept that triggers a callback to a collaborator server.

VULNERABILITY_ID: DeepSeek TUI: run_tests Tool Enables RCE via Malicious Repository Without Approval The run_tests tool in DeepSeek TUI executes cargo test with ApprovalRequirement::Auto, so it runs without a user approval prompt. Because cargo test compiles and executes test binaries, build.rs scripts and proc macros, a malicious repository can run arbitrary shell commands with no approval, and the source states AGENTS.md can instruct the model to call run_tests at session start.

VULNERABILITY_ID: DeepSeek TUI has SSRF via HTTP Redirect Bypass in fetch_url Tool DeepSeek TUI's fetch_url tool checks the initial URL's resolved IP against an is_restricted_ip() blocklist, but its reqwest HTTP client follows up to five redirects without re-validating each target. A public URL that redirects to 169.254.169.254 therefore reaches the restricted address, and the researcher confirmed a 302 redirect was followed to that IP and to an attacker-controlled host. On cloud-hosted instances, prompt injection can drive this to exfiltrate IAM credentials and instance metadata.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI: LDAP and OAuth First-User Race Condition Allows Multiple Admin Accounts Open WebUI's LDAP and OAuth authentication flows determine a new user's role before inserting the user, creating a time-of-check-time-of-use race on fresh instances. Concurrent first-login requests can all observe an empty user table and all receive the admin role, while the signup handler had already been patched against this pattern. The LDAP and OAuth paths were not updated, so any user who times a first login concurrently with the legitimate first admin can gain full admin privileges, including access to user data, system configuration, API keys, and connected LLM backends.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI: shared-chat branch ignores access_type, allowing unauthorized file deletion Any authenticated Open WebUI user can permanently delete files owned by other users through DELETE /api/v1/files/{id} when the file is referenced in any shared chat. The has_access_to_file() function in backend/open_webui/routers/files.py grants access through its shared-chat branch without checking the requesting user's identity or the access_type operation. File UUIDs are exposed to users with read access to a knowledge base via GET /api/v1/knowledge/{id}/files, and the flaw was tested on version 0.8.3.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI: Unauthenticated endpoint can trigger embedding generation (cost/DoS) Open WebUI's GET /api/v1/memories/ef endpoint runs request.app.state.EMBEDDING_FUNCTION("hello world") without any authentication check, so unauthenticated callers can trigger embedding generation. Because repeated requests consume CPU or GPU resources and can generate charges on a paid remote embedding provider, the flaw enables cost exposure and denial of service.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI: Cross-User File Access via Unchecked file_id in Folder Knowledge and Knowledge-Base Attach Endpoints Multiple Open WebUI endpoints accept a user-supplied `file_id` and attach that file to a resource the caller controls without checking the caller's access to the file. Path 1 is `POST /api/v1/folders/{id}/update` through the folder knowledge consumer in `backend/open_webui/utils/middleware.py`, where the referenced file becomes RAG context for chat completions. Path 2 is the knowledge-base attach endpoints in `backend/open_webui/routers/knowledge.py`, which grant read and write access to the file through `/api/v1/files/{id}/content` and `/api/v1/files/{id}/data/content/update`. An authenticated user who knows another user's file UUID can exfiltrate that file, and on Path 2 also overwrite it.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI Vulnerable to IDOR: Retrieval API Bypasses Knowledge Base Access Controls Open WebUI's `_validate_collection_access()` checks only the `user-memory-*` and `file-*` collection name prefixes, so knowledge base collections named with raw UUIDs pass unchecked. Any authenticated non-admin user who knows a private knowledge base UUID can read its content through the `/api/v1/retrieval/query/doc` and `/api/v1/retrieval/query/collection` endpoints. The same gap lets an attacker write to another user's knowledge base through the `/api/v1/retrieval/process/*` endpoints, including overwriting content.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI Vulnerable to Unauthenticated RAG Configuration Disclosure VULNERABILITY_ID affects Open WebUI's `main` branch, confirmed unpatched through v0.9.2. The `get_status()` handler in `backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py`, served at `GET /api/v1/retrieval/`, lacks an authentication dependency, so any unauthenticated client can read live RAG configuration. The disclosed fields include the RAG template, embedding engine and model, reranking model, and chunk size and overlap.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI: Authenticated users can bypass model access control via exposed query parameter [AI-ASSISTED] VULNERABILITY_ID affects Open WebUI. The bypass_filter parameter in the generate_chat_completion handlers in routers/openai.py and routers/ollama.py is bound from the query string by FastAPI, so an authenticated user can append ?bypass_filter=true to /openai/chat/completions or /ollama/api/chat. This skips the model access control check, letting any authenticated user invoke admin-restricted models through the server's configured connections.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI Exposes System Prompt to Regular User [Non-Admin] A regular, non-admin user of Open WebUI v0.6.40 (the "main" branch) can see the system prompts that an admin set for models. The GET /api/models? response, which the application requests automatically at login, includes the system prompt of every available model configured on the workspace models pages. The source states the impact as exposing model instructions and enabling content manipulation of model input and output.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI Has Stored Cross-Site Scripting in SVG Renderer A stored cross-site scripting flaw exists in the SVG renderer of Open WebUI, tracked as VULNERABILITY_ID. An authenticated user can edit a generated SVG and append an img element with an onerror handler, and the code runs when the image is saved and rendered. The malicious thread can be shared with other users or administrators, which the report says can expose sensitive data or lead to account takeover.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI's API key endpoint restrictions bypassed via `x-api-key` header — full message processing on restricted endpoints Open WebUI's Anthropic-compatible API path accepts API keys via the `x-api-key` header, but endpoint restrictions are checked only for keys sent in the `Authorization` header. A key restricted from `/api/v1/messages` returns 403 with `Authorization: Bearer sk-...`, yet the same key sent via `x-api-key` is authenticated and returns a full model response. The advisory's proof of concept was verified against Open WebUI v0.8.11, and the bypass lets any restricted key reach any endpoint.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Missing integrity verification in the Triton inference handler in Amazon SageMaker Python SDK v2 before v2.257.2 and v3… Missing integrity verification in the Triton inference handler in Amazon SageMaker Python SDK v2 before v2.257.2 and v3 before v3.8.0 lets a remote authenticated actor with S3 write access to the model artifact path replace model artifacts with a crafted pickle payload. The payload is deserialized without verification, allowing code execution in inference containers.

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: Hatchet is a platform for orchestrating background tasks, AI agents, and durable workflows at scale. Prior to 0.83.39… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Hatchet, a platform for orchestrating background tasks, AI agents, and durable workflows, prior to 0.83.39. A missing authorization directive on the GET /api/v1/stable/dags/tasks endpoint skipped the tenant-membership check, so a user authenticated to any tenant on the same instance could supply another tenant's UUID and a DAG UUID from that tenant and receive that DAG's task metadata.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI: Evaluator create+update mass-assignment allows cross-workspace evaluator takeover FlowiseAI's Evaluator create and update handlers in `packages/server/src/Interface.Evaluation.ts` copy the request body onto the entity with `Object.assign(newEvaluator, body)` and no field allowlist. A client-supplied `workspaceId` therefore persists on the row, letting any authenticated workspace member move an evaluator into another workspace.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI: Evaluation create+update mass-assignment allows cross-workspace evaluation takeover FlowiseAI's Evaluation create and update paths copy the request body into the entity with Object.assign(...) and no field allowlist. An authenticated workspace member can therefore send a workspaceId in the body, which is persisted and moves the evaluation into another workspace, along with any data it holds. The source says the flaw is fixed in PR 6050 using an allowlist pattern, matching the DocumentStore fix in commit 840d2ae.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI: DatasetRow create+update mass-assignment allows cross-workspace row takeover VULNERABILITY_ID affects FlowiseAI's DatasetRow create and update paths in packages/server/src/services/dataset/index.ts. The code copies the request body onto the entity with Object.assign without a field allowlist, so a client-supplied workspaceId persists on the row. An authenticated workspace member can move a datasetrow into another workspace, exposing its contents there, and the source does not describe the fix's specific version beyond the referenced pull request.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI: Dataset create+update mass-assignment allows cross-workspace dataset takeover FlowiseAI's dataset service copies the request body into the Dataset entity with Object.assign(), without a field allowlist. An authenticated workspace member can therefore set workspaceId (and id on create) through the request, moving a dataset into another workspace and exposing its rows and schema to that workspace. The affected file is packages/server/src/services/dataset/index.ts, and the flaw is described as with no second factor needed.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI: CustomTemplate create+update mass-assignment allows cross-workspace template takeover The FlowiseAI CustomTemplate create and update paths in packages/server/src/services/marketplaces/index.ts copy the full request body onto the entity with Object.assign(newTemplate, body) and no field allowlist. A client-supplied workspaceId, and on create an id, is therefore persisted, letting any authenticated member who can edit a customtemplate move it into another workspace by UUID. The advisory notes that workspace UUIDs are often exposed in API responses, which makes target enumeration simple.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI: Assistant create+update mass-assignment allows cross-workspace assistant takeover FlowiseAI's Assistant create and update paths copy the request body onto the entity with Object.assign without a field allowlist. An authenticated workspace member can therefore set workspaceId, and on create also id, to move an assistant into another workspace. The source states the flaw is fixed in PR 6128, which applies an allowlist pattern.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI: Vector Store No Permission Checks FlowiseAI's OpenAI Assistants vector store routes at packages/server/src/routes/openai-assistants-vector-store/index.ts have no checkAnyPermission() middleware on any CRUD operation. Any authenticated user, regardless of role, can create, update, or delete vector stores, upload files to them, and delete files. The source () under CWE-306 and says the impact includes uploading malicious files and exfiltrating stored documents.

VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n Has a Cross-user Authorization Bypass in Dynamic Credential OAuth Endpoints The OAuth1 and OAuth2 credential reconnect endpoints in n8n authorized access using `credential:read` instead of `credential:update`. An authenticated user with read-only access to a shared credential could start a reconnect flow and overwrite its stored tokens with ones tied to an external account they control, so workflows using that credential would run under the attacker's identity. The issue affects instances where credentials are shared with other users or across projects.

VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n: HTTP Request Node Pagination Prototype Pollution to RCE An authenticated user who can create or modify workflows can trigger global prototype pollution in n8n through an unvalidated pagination parameter in the HTTP Request node. Combined with other techniques, this can lead to RCE on the instance.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI Vulnerable to Credential Data Leak FlowiseAI's credentials service returns the encryptedData field when credentials are fetched with a credentialName filter, because the omit step runs only for unfiltered requests (packages/server/src/services/credentials/index.ts, lines 62-71). Authenticated users can read encrypted API keys, passwords and tokens for services such as OpenAI and AWS. The source says combining this with the encryption key file at ~/.flowise/encryption.key, written with default permissions, enables full credential theft.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI: Authenticated Host RCE via POST /api/v1/node-custom-function and NodeVM Sandbox Escape Flowise's POST /api/v1/node-custom-function endpoint has no route-level permission middleware, so any authenticated user or API key can submit arbitrary JavaScript to the Custom JS Function node. When E2B_APIKEY is unset, which the source describes as the common deployment case, the code runs in a NodeVM sandbox that can be escaped by abusing an Error object that crosses the sandbox boundary to recover the host Function constructor. The attacker then reaches process and child_process and runs system commands on the server host.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI has Mass Assignment in Assistant Update Endpoint that Allows Cross-Workspace Resource Reassignment An authenticated user can exploit a Mass Assignment flaw in the PUT /api/v1/assistants/{assistantId} endpoint of FlowiseAI. The server does not restrict which properties the client may modify, so requests can change server-controlled fields such as workspaceId, createdDate and updatedDate. This allows an attacker to reassign assistants to arbitrary workspaces, breaking tenant isolation in multi-workspace deployments.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise has an MCP Security Bypass that Enables RCE Flowise's MCP feature contains a security bypass chain that lets an attacker run arbitrary commands on the host. The validateCommandFlags blocklist in packages/components/nodes/tools/MCP/core.ts omits docker build, so a Custom MCP Server configured as docker build <remote-URL> pulls and runs a remote Dockerfile. A second bypass uses the long alias --yes, which is not blocked for npx, letting npx install and execute an attacker-supplied npm package. The attacker needs a Flowise account of any role or an API key with view and update permissions for chatflows, and the server must have the docker or npx command available.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI Exposes Basic Auth Credentials via API A Kolega.dev Deep Code Scan flagged the checkBasicAuth endpoint in FlowiseAI at packages/server/src/enterprise/controllers/account.controller.ts:128-135 as under CWE-522 (Insufficiently Protected Credentials). The endpoint compares plaintext username and password from the request body directly against the FLOWISE_USERNAME and FLOWISE_PASSWORD environment variables, with no rate limiting and different responses for success and failure. Attackers can therefore attempt unlimited credential brute-forcing and enumerate valid credentials.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI has Mass Assignment in Chatflow Update Endpoint that Allows Cross-Workspace AgentFlow Reassignment A mass assignment flaw in the PUT /api/v1/chatflows/{chatflowId} endpoint of FlowiseAI lets an authenticated user set server-controlled fields such as deployed, isPublic, workspaceId, createdDate and updatedDate, because the request body is merged directly into the chatflow model without a DTO whitelist or authorization checks. In testing, a chatflow was reassigned to a second workspace, which breaks tenant isolation in multi-tenant deployments and may expose private workflows or alter deployed agent workflows.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI has Mass Assignment in Tool Update Endpoint that Allows Cross-Workspace Resource Reassignment FlowiseAI's tool update endpoint, PUT /api/v1/tools/{toolId}, merges the client's JSON body directly into the database entity without DTO validation or authorization checks. An authenticated user can therefore set server-controlled fields such as workspaceId, createdDate and updatedDate, moving tools into arbitrary workspaces and breaking tenant isolation in multi-workspace deployments.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FlowiseAI has Mass Assignment in Variable Update Endpoint that Allows Cross-Workspace Resource Reassignment VULNERABILITY_ID describes a Mass Assignment flaw in the FlowiseAI variable update endpoint, PUT /api/v1/variables/{variableId}. Authenticated users can send server-controlled fields such as workspaceId, createdDate and updatedDate, and the backend persists them without validation or authorization checks. An attacker can therefore reassign variables to arbitrary workspaces, which may break tenant isolation in multi-workspace deployments.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LangSmith SDK: Public prompt pull deserializes untrusted manifests without trust boundary warning The LangSmith SDK's prompt pull methods (`pull_prompt` / `pull_prompt_commit` in Python, `pullPrompt` / `pullPromptCommit` in JS/TS) deserialize prompt manifests from the LangSmith Hub without distinguishing public prompts pulled by `owner/name` from prompts within the caller's own organization. A malicious or compromised publisher can supply manifests that instantiate LangChain objects with attacker-chosen constructor arguments, such as an LLM `base_url`, which can redirect traffic and expose prompts, credentials and other secrets, or alter model behavior.

VULNERABILITY_ID: nnU-Net is a semantic segmentation framework that automatically adapts its pipeline to a dataset. Prior to 2.4.1, the… VULNERABILITY_ID affects nnU-Net, a semantic segmentation framework, before version 2.4.1. Its Issue Triage workflow in.github/workflows/issue-triage.yml sets allowed_non_write_users to the issue author's login, so any logged-in GitHub user who opens an issue can reach the workflow. Untrusted issue title and body text is embedded directly into the prompt of anthropics/claude-code-action, which runs a command-capable Claude agent that can comment on and relabel the issue via gh, and the workflow triggers automatically on issues.opened. An external attacker can therefore submit a crafted issue that steers the agent beyond issue triage and influences authenticated issue actions.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in M365 Copilot allows an… VULNERABILITY_ID is classified as CWE-77, Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection'), in M365 Copilot. The source states that an unauthorized attacker can perform tampering over a network. NVD had not yet provided an assessment at the time of the record.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow is a tool for building and deploying AI-powered agents and workflows. Prior to 1.9.0, Langflow is vulnerable… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Langflow versions prior to 1.9.0 in the Knowledge Bases API (DELETE /api/v1/knowledge_bases). User-supplied knowledge base names are concatenated directly into file paths without sanitization or boundary validation.
