As a result, the BIP-39 seed was embedded in the LLM tool-call JSON and exposed to any transport, log or telemetry surface between the LLM provider and the MCP process.

VULNERABILITY_ID: JunoClaw is an agentic AI platform built on Juno Network. Prior to 0.x.y-security-1, substring-based blocklist in… VULNERABILITY_ID affects JunoClaw, an agentic AI platform built on Juno Network, before 0.x.y-security-1. A substring-based blocklist in the plugin-shell command-safety check, applied to the raw command string rather than the parsed first token, can be bypassed by adversarial argument constructions. When combined with the companion advisory, this allows unauthorized command execution on the host.

VULNERABILITY_ID: JunoClaw is an agentic AI platform built on Juno Network. Prior to 0.x.y-security-1, plugin-shell's run_command wrapped… VULNERABILITY_ID affects JunoClaw, an agentic AI platform built on Juno Network, prior to 0.x.y-security-1. The plugin-shell run_command function wrapped every agent-supplied command in 'sh -c' / 'cmd /C' and passed the full argument string to the shell parser, so shell metacharacters in agent-supplied arguments were interpreted as command syntax. The issue is classified as CWE-77 and CWE-78, and NVD published it on 05/12/2026.

VULNERABILITY_ID: JunoClaw is an agentic AI platform built on Juno Network. Prior to 0.x.y-security-1, the upload_wasm MCP tool accepted… VULNERABILITY_ID affects JunoClaw, an agentic AI platform built on Juno Network, prior to 0.x.y-security-1. The upload_wasm MCP tool accepted a filesystem path from the agent and uploaded whatever bytes that path resolved to, without validating location, symlink target, file size, or file format. The flaw is classified as CWE-20, CWE-22, CWE-59 and CWE-73.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaude Sandbox Bypass via Model-Controlled `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` Input VULNERABILITY_ID reports that OpenClaude's BashTool input schema exposes `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` to the model, which the project's own threat model treats as an untrusted principal. In `shouldUseSandbox()` in `src/tools/BashTool/shouldUseSandbox.ts`, that flag skips the sandbox when `areUnsandboxedCommandsAllowed()` returns true, and that check defaults to true in `src/utils/sandbox/sandbox-adapter.ts`. A prompt-injected model can therefore set the flag in a `tool_use` block and run arbitrary host commands under default configuration.

VULNERABILITY_ID: DeepChat is an open-source artificial intelligence agent platform that unifies models, tools, and agents. Prior to… VULNERABILITY_ID affects DeepChat, an open-source AI agent platform, prior to v1.0.4-beta.1. An incomplete fix for VULNERABILITY_ID left native Electron pop-up window handlers unsanitized, so a malicious Markdown link with target="_blank" can route a URL through tabPresenter.ts directly to shell.openExternal(url), bypassing the isValidExternalUrl check. A compromised AI endpoint or attacker can trigger this, enabling arbitrary protocol execution.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A weakness has been identified in aiwaves-cn agents up to e8c4e3c2d19739d3dff59e577d1c97090cc15f59. Affected by this… A weakness in the recall_relevant_memories_to_working_memory function, in core/cat/looking_glass/stray_cat.py of the cheshire_cat_core component of aiwaves-cn agents, affects versions up to e8c4e3c2d19739d3dff59e577d1c97090cc15f59. Manipulating the function causes resource consumption and can be exploited remotely. A public exploit exists, and the project was informed through an issue report but has not yet responded.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SOCFortress CoPilot focuses on providing a single pane of glass for all your security operations needs. Prior to… VULNERABILITY_ID affects SOCFortress CoPilot before 0.1.57. The backend ships a hardcoded JWT signing secret as a fallback in backend/app/auth/utils.py:28 and repeats it in.env.example. Deployments that leave JWT_SECRET unset, including the default Docker Compose setup, sign every authentication token with this public value, letting an unauthenticated attacker forge admin-scoped JWTs and take full control of the application and the security tools it manages.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Dockerfile command injection via envs[*].name in bentofile.yaml (sibling fix-bypass of VULNERABILITY_ID and VULNERABILITY_ID) A crafted bentofile.yaml with a newline-injected envs[*].name value makes the BentoML-generated Dockerfile contain unquoted RUN directives, which execute on the build host when the victim runs bentoml containerize on the imported bento. The flaw is in base_v2.j2 lines 71-73, where env.name is interpolated without bash_quote, and it affects bentoml 1.4.38 (verified) and likely all 1.x versions with _bentoml_impl/docker.py. It is a sibling of VULNERABILITY_ID and VULNERABILITY_ID, whose fixes covered only system_packages.

VULNERABILITY_ID: BentoML Dockerfile command injection via docker.base_image (sister of pending VULNERABILITY_ID / VULNERABILITY_ID / VULNERABILITY_ID) VULNERABILITY_ID reports that the BentoML Dockerfile template interpolates `docker.base_image` without escaping, newline filtering, or validation. A malicious bento.yaml with a multi-line `docker.base_image` value injects extra Dockerfile directives, and `bentoml containerize` runs `docker build`, which executes the injected `RUN` directives on the victim host. The source describes this as a sister issue to pending VULNERABILITY_ID.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI's Improper Authorization in Standard Channels Allows Message Updates with Read Permission In standard channels of Open WebUI, the endpoint POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}/update checks only read permission. When access_control is None, the has_access(..., type="read") check passes, so any authenticated user who is not the message owner can update other users' messages. The source lists the attacker's prerequisites as an authenticated user with role user or higher, a standard channel, and the ability to obtain the target message_id.

Prior to version 4.14.17, FastGPT had an inconsistent SSRF protection gap in… FastGPT, an AI Agent building platform, prior to version 4.14.17, let authenticated users who can create or manage MCP toolsets save an internal MCP server URL, such as http://localhost:3000/mcp, through the MCP tool create and update endpoints. VULNERABILITY_ID: LangChain vulnerable to unsafe deserialization of attacker-controlled objects through overly broad `load()` allowlists LangChain's older runtime code paths deserialize run inputs, run outputs, and other application-controlled payloads using overly broad allowlists, sometimes calling `load()` with `allowed_objects="all"`. Attacker-supplied LangChain serialized constructor dictionaries can therefore cause trusted classes to be instantiated with untrusted constructor arguments, when the application accepts untrusted structured input and preserves it in run data. A related `_is_lc_secret` validation bypass in the serialization layer provides an additional path to the same revival logic.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI has Improper Authorization Control Open WebUI version 0.1.105 has an improper authorization flaw (CWE-285) in which accounts with the pending role can make authenticated API calls as a user. The role check is enforced only at the client presentation layer, while the API does not validate that the user holds the user role. A pending user who signs up through POST /api/v1/auths/signup receives a valid JWT and can call the authenticated GET /ollama/api/tags endpoint to list available models.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Cline Kanban Server has a Cross-Origin WebSocket Hijacking Vulnerability The kanban npm package, used by the cline CLI, runs a WebSocket server on 127.0.0.1:3484 that does not validate the Origin header on its upgrade requests. Any website a developer visits can connect to the runtime, terminal I/O and control endpoints, leaking workspace paths, task details and agent chat messages. A page can also write input into a running agent's terminal, which the source says leads to remote code execution, or stop active agent sessions. Tested against version 0.1.59.

An authenticated MCP caller can supply crafted identifiers that the n8n API client uses as URL path segments, sending the configured n8n API key to other same-origin endpoints and bypassing handler-level controls including DISABLED_TOOLS. Validated webhook, form and chat trigger URLs also follow redirects, returning the response body to the caller, and default opt-in telemetry uploads unredacted operation payloads that can contain bearer tokens, API keys and webhook secrets.; exploitation requires an authenticated MCP caller and a configured n8n API key.

A caller with an MCP session can make the n8n-mcp host send requests to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints, and the response body is returned to the caller. Fixed in n8n-mcp@2.50.2.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PromptHub is an all-in-one AI toolbox for prompt, skill, and agent management. The private-address check in isPrivateIPv6 in apps/web/src/utils/remote-http.ts can be bypassed with alternate IPv6 representations, letting any authenticated user reach IPv4 loopback, RFC1918 and link-local addresses and read up to 5 MB of the response. On deployments with ALLOW_REGISTRATION=true, any internet user who can register can exploit it.

VULNERABILITY_ID: utcp-http vulnerable to SSRF via attacker-controlled OpenAPI servers[0].url in HTTP communication protocol The utcp-http plugin, version 1.1.1 and earlier, contains a blind SSRF flaw. register_manual() checks discovery URLs against an HTTPS or loopback allowlist, but call_tool() and call_tool_streaming() use the resolved tool_call_template.url without revalidating it, so an attacker-hosted OpenAPI spec can declare internal addresses such as http://169.254.169.254 in servers[0].url. A prefix check also let http://localhost.evil.com bypass the loopback rule. The flaw affects the utcp_http.http, utcp_http.streamable_http and utcp_http.sse protocols and can expose cloud metadata and internal services to the LLM caller.

VULNERABILITY_ID: BentoML has Information Disclosure in `bentoml build` via symlink traversal in the build context BentoML's `bentoml build` packaging workflow follows symlinks inside the build context and copies the referenced file contents into the generated Bento artifact. The `os.walk` loop in the packaging code calls `shutil.copy` without checking that the resolved path stays inside `ctx_path`. An attacker who gets a developer or CI system to build an attacker-controlled repository can exfiltrate local files such as cloud credentials or SSH keys, and the leak can spread through export, push, or containerization. The issue was verified against BentoML 1.4.38.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Diffusers has a `trust_remote_code` bypass via `custom_pipeline` and local custom components Diffusers versions before 0.38.0 let `DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained` execute remote code even when `trust_remote_code=False` or omitted. The `trust_remote_code` gate sat inside `DiffusionPipeline.download()`, so cross-repo `custom_pipeline` values and local snapshots, which skip `download()`, loaded and ran attacker-supplied `pipeline.py` or custom component files silently on the victim's machine. Anyone calling `from_pretrained` with custom pipelines is affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Duplicate Advisory: Diffusers has a `trust_remote_code` bypass via `custom_pipeline` and local custom components This advisory was withdrawn as a duplicate of VULNERABILITY_ID and is kept to preserve external references. A body-supplied org_id could override the authenticated org, letting one tenant's requests be recorded in another tenant's audit log and evaluated under the wrong policy set.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Keras vulnerable to DoS via Malicious.keras Model (HDF5 Shape Bomb Causes Petabyte Allocation in KerasFileEditor) The Keras model loader, KerasFileEditor, reads HDF5 weight files inside user-supplied.keras archives without validating dataset metadata. A crafted model.weights.h5 declaring a dataset shape of (50000000, 50000000) with only a few bytes of stored data triggers a full-shape allocation via value[()] in h5py, producing an attempted 8.88 PiB allocation that crashes the process. The advisory describes the impact as denial of service for any environment or pipeline that loads untrusted.keras models.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI has unauthenticated RCE via `tool_override.py` (VULNERABILITY_ID patch bypass) VULNERABILITY_ID's fix gated tools.py auto-import behind PRAISONAI_ALLOW_LOCAL_TOOLS=true in tool_resolver.py and api/call.py, but a third import sink in praisonai/templates/tool_override.py was not patched. Because the recipe runner reaches that sink on every recipe execution, POST /v1/recipes/run with a recipe value pointing at a local absolute path or a GitHub repo can cause the server to exec_module() an attacker-supplied tools.py, with no authentication or environment opt-in required by default, since SecurityConfig.allow_any_github defaults to True. The source reports a confirmed execution against praisonai 4.6.31 on 2026-04-25.

VULNERABILITY_ID: rmcp Streamable HTTP server transport has a DNS rebinding vulnerability Prior to version 1.4.0, the rmcp crate's Streamable HTTP server transport did not validate the incoming Host header, so a malicious public website using a DNS rebinding attack could send authenticated requests to a local or private-network MCP server. An attacker could enumerate and invoke exposed tools and read resources, and because MCP servers often run with the user's privileges, the impact can extend to arbitrary code execution on the victim's machine.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM: extract_hidden_states speculative decoding crashes server on any request with penalty parameters A shape regression in vLLM's extract_hidden_states speculative decoding proposer, introduced when the KV connector interface was refactored in PR #37013, causes a RuntimeError that crashes the EngineCore process. Any request containing repetition_penalty, frequency_penalty, or presence_penalty triggers the crash, affecting deployments from v0.18.0 through v0.19.1 inclusive.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Nginx-UI Settings API Exposes Protected Secrets The GetSettings handler in api/settings/settings.go serializes every settings struct to JSON for any authenticated user. The protected:"true" tag is enforced only on writes through ProtectedFill in SaveSettings, so more than 40 protected fields, including JwtSecret, NodeSecret, OIDC ClientSecret and the IPWhiteList configuration, are returned on read. Exposed secrets allow forging auth tokens, impersonating cluster nodes and performing OAuth flows as the application.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM Vulnerable to Remote DoS via Special-Token Placeholders Unauthenticated text-only prompts in vLLM that spell special tokens such as <|image_pad|> are interpreted as control tokens. When image or video placeholders arrive without matching data, get_input_positions_tensor in vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding.py indexes empty image_grid_thw/video_grid_thw grids without a bounds check, raising an unhandled IndexError that can terminate the worker. Reproduced on vLLM 0.10.0 with Qwen2.5-VL; a single request can trigger it.

VULNERABILITY_ID: ciguard: discover_pipeline_files follows symlinks out of scan root The discover_pipeline_files() function in src/ciguard/discovery.py, introduced in v0.8.0 and used by the MCP scan_repo tool in v0.8.1, follows symlinks during directory walks. An attacker who can plant a symlink in a scanned directory can make discovery return pipeline-shaped files outside the requested root, and an AI agent driven by an adversarial prompt can then read their content through later scan calls.
