VULNERABILITY_ID: kedro-datasets has a path traversal vulnerability in PartitionedDataset that allows arbitrary file write PartitionedDataset in kedro-datasets concatenated partition IDs directly onto the dataset base path without validation, so partition IDs containing.. components could write files outside the configured directory and overwrite arbitrary files on the filesystem. All storage backends, including local filesystem, S3 and GCS, are affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A flaw has been found in Ollama up to 18.1. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file server/download.go… VULNERABILITY_ID is a flaw in Ollama up to 18.1, located in the processing of server/download.go within the Model Pull API. Manipulating this processing can lead to server-side request forgery, and the attack can be launched remotely. The vendor was contacted early about the disclosure but did not respond.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Directus: Sensitive fields exposed in revision history Directus stores revision records in `directus_revisions` when items are created or updated, but its revision snapshot code does not consistently pass data through `prepareDelta`. As a result, sensitive fields such as `token`, `tfa_secret`, `external_identifier`, `auth_data`, `credentials`, and AI provider API keys can be stored in plaintext. The payload redaction list used by Flows also omits these fields for `directus_users` operations, so they are written unredacted into flow logs. Any user or service account with read access to `directus_revisions` or flow logs can retrieve these values, which could enable account takeover or unauthorized use of third-party API keys.
affected_vendors_raw: Directus; AI provider API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google)

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: @mobilenext/mobile-mcp: Arbitrary Android Intent Execution via mobile_open_url The mobile_open_url tool in @mobilenext/mobile-mcp passes user-supplied URLs straight to Android's intent system through adb shell am start without scheme validation. Because MCP servers are driven by AI agents that can be manipulated through prompt injection, a malicious document or website could make the agent open tel:, sms:, mailto:, content:// or market:// URLs, enabling USSD codes, calls, SMS drafts, content provider access and app installation prompts.

VULNERABILITY_ID: BentoML: SSTI via Unsandboxed Jinja2 in Dockerfile Generation BentoML's generate_containerfile() in src/bentoml/_internal/container/generate.py renders user-supplied dockerfile_template files with an unsandboxed jinja2.Environment that loads the jinja2.ext.do and jinja2.ext.debug extensions. A malicious bento archive containing a crafted template runs arbitrary Python on the host when a victim imports it and runs bentoml containerize, before any Docker container is created, bypassing container isolation.

VULNERABILITY_ID: BentoML: Command Injection in cloud deployment setup script BentoML's commit ce53491 added shlex.quote to fix command injection via system_packages in Dockerfile templates and images.py, but the cloud deployment path in src/bentoml/_internal/cloud/deployment.py was left out. Line 1648 of that file joins system_packages values from bentofile.yaml into an apt-get install shell command with an f-string and no quoting. The generated setup.sh is uploaded to BentoCloud and run on the cloud build infrastructure, so a malicious bentofile.yaml can execute arbitrary commands there during deployment, including during Deployment.watch() dev-mode deployments.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LiteLLM: Authentication bypass via OIDC userinfo cache key collision LiteLLM's OIDC userinfo cache keys JWT tokens by their first 20 characters (`token[:20]`) when `enable_jwt_auth: true` is set. Because tokens from the same signing algorithm share identical leading characters, an unauthenticated attacker can craft a token that hits a legitimate user's cache entry and inherits that user's identity and permissions. The option is not enabled by default, so most instances are not affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LiteLLM: Privilege escalation via unrestricted proxy configuration endpoint LiteLLM's /config/update endpoint does not enforce admin role authorization, so any authenticated user can reach it. From there, an attacker can change proxy configuration and environment variables, register pass-through endpoint handlers that run attacker-controlled Python code (remote code execution), read arbitrary server files via UI_LOGO_PATH and /get_image, and take over privileged accounts by overwriting UI_USERNAME and UI_PASSWORD.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Mesop: Unbounded Thread Creation in WebSocket Handler Leads to Denial of Service The Mesop framework's WebSocket handler, `handle_websocket` in `mesop/server/server.py`, starts a new `threading.Thread` for every parsed `ui_request` with no thread pool, message queue or rate limit. An unauthenticated attacker can send a rapid stream of messages over one connection to exhaust threads and memory, causing a denial of service for applications built on the framework.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM: Denial of Service via Unbounded Frame Count in video/jpeg Base64 Processing The `VideoMediaIO.load_base64()` method in vLLM (`vllm/multimodal/media/video.py`) splits `video/jpeg` data URLs on commas without any frame count limit, bypassing the `num_frames` default of 32 enforced on the `load_bytes()` path. A single request to `/v1/chat/completions` containing thousands of base64-encoded JPEG frames causes the server to decode them all into memory and crash with an out-of-memory condition.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in `download_bytes_from_url ` A server-side request forgery flaw in the `download_bytes_from_url` function of vLLM's batch runner (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/run_batch.py`) lets anyone who controls batch input JSON make the server issue arbitrary HTTP or HTTPS requests. The function applies no hostname, IP, port or redirect validation, unlike the multimodal `MediaConnector` path, which uses a domain allowlist. The `file_url` field of the batch transcription and translation request models feeds the URL directly, so internal services such as cloud metadata endpoints reachable from the vLLM host can be targeted.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw before 2026.4.2 reuses the PKCE verifier as the OAuth state parameter in the Gemini OAuth flow, exposing it… VULNERABILITY_ID affects OpenClaw before 2026.4.2. In the Gemini OAuth flow, it reuses the PKCE verifier as the OAuth state parameter, which exposes the verifier through the redirect URL. An attacker who captures that redirect URL can obtain both the authorization code and the PKCE verifier, defeating PKCE protection and enabling token redemption.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastMCP is the standard framework for building MCP applications. Prior to version 3.2.0, server names containing shell… VULNERABILITY_ID affects FastMCP, a framework for building MCP applications, before version 3.2.0. On Windows, server names containing shell metacharacters such as & can trigger command injection when passed to fastmcp install claude-code or fastmcp install gemini-cli. The install paths call subprocess.run() with a list argument, but target CLIs that resolve to.cmd wrappers run through cmd.exe, which interprets the metacharacters in the flattened command string.
affected_vendors_raw: FastMCP; MCP; Claude Code; Gemini CLI

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM: Unauthenticated OOM Denial of Service via Unbounded `n` Parameter in OpenAI API Server The vLLM OpenAI-compatible API server has a denial-of-service flaw in the `n` parameter of `ChatCompletionRequest` and `CompletionRequest`. These Pydantic models set no upper bound on `n`, and `_verify_args` in `vllm/sampling_params.py` checks only the lower bound, so an unauthenticated attacker can send one request with a very large `n`. The engine in `vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py` then fans the request out into millions of copies, blocking the asyncio event loop and driving memory use up until the OS OOM-killer terminates the process.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw: Fake DeviceToken Bypasses Shared Auth Rate Limiting OpenClaw's npm package `openclaw` contains a flaw in its shared authentication flow over WebSocket, where a fake DeviceToken bypasses shared auth rate limiting. The vulnerable range is `<=2026.3.28`. Maintainers note practical risk is mostly limited to deployments that use weak shared passwords, since strong shared tokens remain non-bruteforceable.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw: Agentic Consent Bypass — LLM Agent Can Silently Disable Exec Approval via `config.patch` OpenClaw's openclaw npm package, versions <=2026.3.24, lets an LLM agent silently disable exec approval through the config.patch function, bypassing user consent for command execution. Maintainers fixed it in commit 76411b2afc4ae721e36c12e0ea24fd23e2fed61e, shipped in v2026.3.28, and severity.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs). From version 0.5.5 to before version 0.18.0… vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models, versions 0.5.5 to before 0.18.0, uses Librosa's default numpy.mean for mono downmixing (to_mono). The ITU-R BS.775-4 standard specifies a weighted downmix, so audio heard by humans differs from audio processed by AI models such as those served by vLLM or Transformers.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface that allows users to interact with text generation large language… SillyTavern versions prior to 1.17.0 contain an SSRF flaw in src/endpoints/search.js. The hostname check, matching /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/, only catches literal dotted-quad IPv4 addresses, so localhost, [::1] and DNS names resolving to internal addresses bypass it. A port check (urlObj.port !== '') limits exploitation to services on default ports 80 and 443, making this lower severity than an unrestricted SSRF.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface that allows users to interact with text generation large language… VULNERABILITY_ID affects SillyTavern versions prior to 1.17.0. A path traversal flaw in the chat endpoints lets an authenticated attacker read and delete arbitrary files under their user data root, such as secrets.json and settings.json, by supplying avatar_url="..". The weakness is classified as CWE-22.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface that allows users to interact with text generation large language… SillyTavern, a locally installed user interface for text generation LLMs, image generation engines and text-to-speech models, is affected by VULNERABILITY_ID in versions prior to 1.17.0. A path traversal flaw in the static file route handler lets any unauthenticated user send percent-encoded %2E%2E%2F sequences to static file routes to check whether files exist anywhere on the server's filesystem.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface that allows users to interact with text generation large language… VULNERABILITY_ID affects SillyTavern, a locally installed user interface for text generation large language models, image generation engines, and text-to-speech voice models, prior to version 1.17.0. An authenticated attacker can inject traversal sequences into character_name in /api/chats/import to write attacker-controlled files outside the intended chats directory. The weakness is classified as CWE-22 and CWE-73.

VULNERABILITY_ID: ONNX: TOCTOU arbitrary file read/write in save_external_dat The ONNX save_external_data method in onnx/external_data_helper.py is reported to contain a local TOCTOU flaw, enabling arbitrary file read and write. Between os.path.isfile and open, the code creates no atomic file and does not use O_NOFOLLOW, so an attacker can swap in a symlink and overwrite victim files under the same privilege scope. A possible path validation bypass on Windows, using absolute paths such as C:\ with a single path part, is described but not verified by the reporter.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI Has SSRF in FileTools.download_file() via Unvalidated URL VULNERABILITY_ID reports an SSRF flaw in FileTools.download_file() in praisonaiagents. The function checks the destination path but passes the caller-supplied url directly to httpx.stream() with follow_redirects=True, so an attacker who controls the URL can reach any host the server can access, including cloud metadata services and internal services. On EC2 instances with IMDSv1 enabled, IAM credentials can be retrieved and written to disk, and the flaw is reachable through indirect prompt injection without authentication.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI Has Sandbox Escape via shell=True and Bypassable Blocklist in SubprocessSandbox In PraisonAI, `SubprocessSandbox` runs commands through `subprocess.run()` with `shell=True` and blocks dangerous commands only by string-pattern matching. The blocklist omits `sh` and `bash`, so in STRICT mode a call such as `sh -c 'id'` escapes the sandbox, and blocked commands like curl, wget, nc and ssh become reachable. Combined with agent prompt injection, an attacker could reach the network, filesystem and cloud metadata services. The source reports testing on praisonai==4.5.87.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI: SSRF via Unvalidated api_base in passthrough() Fallback The praisonai package's passthrough() and apassthrough() functions take a caller-controlled api_base parameter and concatenate it with endpoint, sending the request via httpx.Client.request() when the litellm primary path raises AttributeError. No scheme validation, private IP filtering or domain allowlist is applied, enabling server-side request forgery to any host reachable from the server. On EC2 with IMDSv1, the source says an attacker can retrieve IAM credentials, and internal services such as Redis, Elasticsearch and the Kubernetes API can be reached without authentication from within the VPC.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI: Shell Injection in run_python() via Unescaped $() Substitution PraisonAI's `run_python()` in `praisonai` builds a shell command by placing user-controlled code inside `python3 -c "<code>"` and runs it with `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. Its escaping only handles `\` and `"`, so `$()` and backtick substitutions execute as OS commands before Python starts, enabling arbitrary command execution as the process user. The advisory notes the function is reachable through indirect prompt injection, and the auto-generated Flask server ships with `AUTH_ENABLED = False` when no token is configured.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PraisonAI: Python Sandbox Escape via str Subclass startswith() Override in execute_code The execute_code() function in praisonai-agents runs attacker-controlled Python inside a three-layer sandbox. Passing a str subclass with an overridden startswith() method to the _safe_getattr wrapper bypasses the sandbox, allowing arbitrary OS command execution on the host as the process user. Deployments using bot.py, autonomy_mode.py, or bots_cli.py set PRAISONAI_AUTO_APPROVE=true by default, so the tool can fire without human confirmation when triggered via indirect prompt injection.

VULNERABILITY_ID: DNS Rebinding Protection Disabled by Default in Model Context Protocol Go SDK for Servers Running on Localhost The Model Context Protocol (MCP) Go SDK does not enable DNS rebinding protection by default for HTTP-based servers. A malicious website could use DNS rebinding to bypass same-origin restrictions and send requests to an HTTP-based MCP server running on localhost without authentication, using `StreamableHTTPHandler` or `SSEHandler`. This could let an attacker invoke tools or access resources on the user's behalf, and servers using stdio transport are not affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) is an open standard for machine learning interoperability. Prior to version 1.21.0… VULNERABILITY_ID is a symlink traversal vulnerability in external data loading in the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX). Prior to version 1.21.0, it allows reading files outside the model directory. The source classifies it under CWE-22 and CWE-61 and reports no NVD assessment yet.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) is an open standard for machine learning interoperability. Prior to version 1.21.0… VULNERABILITY_ID affects the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) library before version 1.21.0. The onnx.load function checks for symlinks to prevent path traversal but does not check for hardlinks, which look like regular files on the filesystem, so the protection can be bypassed. The issue is classified as CWE-22 and CWE-61. NVD has not yet provided an assessment.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) is an open standard for machine learning interoperability. Prior to version 1.21.0… VULNERABILITY_ID affects the ExternalDataInfo class in Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) versions prior to 1.21.0. The class passes metadata such as file paths and data lengths from an ONNX model file to Python's setattr() without checking whether the keys are valid. An attacker can craft a malicious model that overwrites internal object properties.

VULNERABILITY_ID: TorchGeo Remote Code Execution Vulnerability TorchGeo versions 0.4 through 0.6.0 used an `eval` statement in its model weight API, which could let an unauthenticated remote attacker execute arbitrary commands. Platforms exposing `torchgeo.models.get_weight()` or `torchgeo.trainers` as an external API could be affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw SSRF guard misses four IPv6 special-use ranges The SSRF/IP classifier in OpenClaw treated four IPv6 special-use ranges as public, so fetches to them were allowed. An attacker who controlled a fetched URL could target internal or non-routable IPv6 addresses that the SSRF guard should have blocked. Affected files are src/shared/net/ip.ts and src/infra/net/ssrf.*, in versions <= 2026.3.24.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw host-env blocklist missing `GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR` and `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` allows code execution via env override The host execution environment sanitization in OpenClaw did not block `GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR` or `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`. An approved exec request could use these variables to redirect git or AWS CLI behavior to attacker-controlled configuration, leading to execution of untrusted code or loading of attacker-selected credentials. Affected versions are `<= 2026.3.24`.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw safeBins jq `$ENV` filter bypass allows environment variable disclosure OpenClaw's safe-bin policy for jq blocked explicit `env` usage but still allowed jq programs to read environment data through `$ENV`. An operator-approved safe-bin jq command could therefore disclose environment variables that the policy was meant to keep out of scope. Affected versions are `<= 2026.3.24`, and the flaw sits in `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-semantics.ts`.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastMCP OpenAPI Provider has an SSRF & Path Traversal Vulnerability VULNERABILITY_ID affects the OpenAPIProvider in FastMCP, which parses OpenAPI specifications to expose internal APIs to MCP clients. The _build_url() method in fastmcp/utilities/openapi/director.py substitutes path parameter values into URL templates without URL-encoding, and urljoin() then resolves../ sequences, letting an attacker reach arbitrary backend endpoints. Because requests carry the MCP provider's configured authorization headers, the flaw results in authenticated SSRF.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastMCP: Missing Consent Verification in OAuth Proxy Callback Facilitates Confused Deputy Vulnerabilities The FastMCP OAuthProxy does not verify user consent when it receives an authorization code from the identity provider, in its _handle_idp_callback function. Because GitHub skips the consent page for previously authorized clients, an attacker can capture a GitHub authorization URL after consenting and lure a logged-in victim to open it. The victim's browser then redirects to the malicious client's callback with a valid authorization code, which the attacker can exchange for an access token to the benign MCP server tied to the victim's GitHub account. The issue was verified only for GitHubProvider, but the flaw affects any OAuth integration whose identity provider skips consent.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastGPT is an AI Agent building platform. Prior to version 4.14.9.5, FastGPT's MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools… FastGPT, an AI Agent building platform, has an SSRF flaw in its MCP tools endpoints, /api/core/app/mcpTools/getTools and /api/core/app/mcpTools/runTool, before version 4.14.9.5. These endpoints accept a user-supplied URL and send server-side HTTP requests to it without checking for internal or private network addresses. The application's isInternalAddress() function exists but these endpoints do not call it. An authenticated attacker can scan internal networks, reach cloud metadata services, and interact with internal services such as MongoDB and Redis.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastGPT is an AI Agent building platform. Prior to version 4.14.9.5, the FastGPT HTTP tools testing endpoint… VULNERABILITY_ID affects FastGPT, an AI Agent building platform, prior to version 4.14.9.5. The HTTP tools testing endpoint /api/core/app/httpTools/runTool is exposed without any authentication and acts as a full HTTP proxy, accepting a user-supplied baseUrl, toolPath, method, headers and body, then returning the complete server-side response to the caller. It is classified as CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function) and CWE-918 (Server-Side Request Forgery).

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw has an Arbitrary Malicious Code Execution Vulnerability OpenClaw's local plugin and hook installation runs `npm install --omit=dev --silent --ignore-scripts` in a staged copy of the source directory without stripping the project-level `.npmrc`. A malicious `.npmrc` can set `git` to a program of the attacker's choice, so when a Git dependency is resolved during install, that program executes arbitrary local code before the plugin or hook is loaded.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw has a Gateway HTTP /v1/models Route Bypasses Operator Read Scope OpenClaw's OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint `/v1/models` accepts bearer auth but does not enforce operator method scopes, while the WebSocket RPC path enforces `operator.read` for `models.list`. A caller holding only `operator.approvals` is rejected over WS with `missing scope: operator.read` but still receives model metadata with status 200 over HTTP `/v1/models`.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw has Sandbox Media Root Bypass via Unnormalized `mediaUrl` / `fileUrl` Parameter Keys (CWE-22) A path traversal flaw in OpenClaw's agent sandbox lets a sandboxed agent read files from other agents' workspaces. The normalizeSandboxMediaParams function in src/infra/outbound/message-action-params.ts only checks the media, path and filePath keys, so mediaUrl and fileUrl bypass sandbox validation. handlePluginAction in src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.ts also omits mediaLocalRoots from the dispatch context, so plugins fall back to default roots that permit reads across the ~/.openclaw/ tree.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A cross-session information disclosure vulnerability exists in the awesome-llm-apps project in commit… VULNERABILITY_ID is a cross-session information disclosure flaw in the awesome-llm-apps project at commit e46690f99c3f08be80a9877fab52acacf7ab8251 (2026-01-19). The Streamlit-based GitHub MCP Agent stores user-supplied API tokens in process-wide environment variables via os.environ without session isolation, so credentials from one user stay readable by later unauthenticated users. An attacker could retrieve GitHub Personal Access Tokens or LLM API keys, enabling unauthorized access to private resources and financial abuse.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability has been found in PromtEngineer localGPT up to 4d41c7d1713b16b216d8e062e51a5dd88b20b054. The impacted… VULNERABILITY_ID affects PromtEngineer localGPT up to commit 4d41c7d1713b16b216d8e062e51a5dd88b20b054. The flaw sits in the function _route_using_overviews in backend/server.py, within the LLM Prompt Handler component, and manipulation there leads to injection. The attack can be performed remotely, and public exploit code may be used.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability has been found in wandb OpenUI up to 0.0.0.0/1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file… VULNERABILITY_ID affects wandb OpenUI up to 0.0.0.0/1.0, in an unknown function of backend/openui/config.py. Manipulating the LITELLM_MASTER_KEY argument leads to hard-coded credentials (CWE-259, CWE-798), and an attack must be launched locally. The exploit is public, and the vendor did not respond to early disclosure contact.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Giskard Agents have Server-side template injection via ChatWorkflow.chat() using non-sandboxed Jinja2 Environment giskard-agents versions up to 0.3.3 and the 1.0.x alpha line pass the string argument of ChatWorkflow.chat() directly into an unsandboxed Jinja2 Environment, so user input is parsed as a template. A developer who passes user input to this method exposes the server to remote code execution through Jinja2 class traversal, which can run system commands, read files and access environment variables.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is a ChatGPT clone with additional features. In versions 0.8.2-rc1 through 0.8.3-rc1, user-created MCP (Model… VULNERABILITY_ID affects LibreChat versions 0.8.2-rc1 through 0.8.3-rc1. User-created MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers can set arbitrary HTTP headers that undergo credential placeholder substitution, so a malicious server using `{{LIBRECHAT_OPENID_ACCESS_TOKEN}}` in its headers can exfiltrate the OAuth tokens of users who call tools on that server. The weakness is classified as CWE-200, Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is a ChatGPT clone with additional features. In versions 0.8.2-rc2 through 0.8.2-rc3, the SSE streaming… VULNERABILITY_ID affects LibreChat in versions 0.8.2-rc2 through 0.8.2-rc3. The SSE streaming endpoint `/api/agents/chat/stream/:streamId` does not check that the requesting user owns the stream, so any authenticated user holding a valid stream ID can subscribe and read another user's real-time chat content, including messages, AI responses and tool invocations. The weakness is classified as CWE-284, Improper Access Control.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is a ChatGPT clone with additional features. Versions 0.8.2-rc2 through 0.8.2 are vulnerable to a server-side… LibreChat versions 0.8.2-rc2 through 0.8.2 are vulnerable to server-side request forgery (SSRF) when agent actions or MCP are used. The earlier fix for VULNERABILITY_ID added hostname validation but does not check whether DNS resolution yields a private IP address, so an attacker can bypass it and reach internal resources such as an internal RAG API or cloud instance metadata endpoints.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is a ChatGPT clone with additional features. Prior to version 0.8.3, `isPrivateIP()` in… VULNERABILITY_ID affects LibreChat before version 0.8.3. The function `isPrivateIP()` in `packages/api/src/auth/domain.ts` fails to detect IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses in hex-normalized form. Any authenticated user can exploit this to bypass SSRF protection and make the server send HTTP requests to internal resources, including cloud metadata services such as `169.254.169.254`, loopback, and RFC1918 ranges.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LangChain Core has Path Traversal vulnerabilites in legacy `load_prompt` functions Multiple functions in `langchain_core.prompts.loading` read files from paths in deserialized config dicts without checking for absolute paths or `..` traversal. When an application passes user-influenced prompt configurations to `load_prompt()` or `load_prompt_from_config()`, an attacker can read arbitrary host files, limited only by `.txt`, `.json`, `.yaml` and `.yml` extension checks.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow: Authenticated Users Can Read, Modify, and Delete Any Flow via Missing Ownership Check Langflow's `_read_flow` helper in `src/backend/base/langflow/api/v1/flows.py` omitted an ownership check when `AUTO_LOGIN` was `False`, so any authenticated user could read, modify, or delete another user's flow via `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/flow/{flow_id}`. Exposed data included embedded plaintext API keys, and attackers could alter other users' AI agent logic. The flaw was introduced by conditional logic meant to support public example flows (`user_id = NULL`) under auto-login mode.

VULNERABILITY_ID: @mobilenext/mobile-mcp alllows arbitrary file write via Path Traversal in mobile screen capture tools The @mobilenext/mobile-mcp server has a path traversal flaw in the mobile_save_screenshot and mobile_start_screen_recording tools. The saveTo and output parameters are passed directly to filesystem write operations (fs.writeFileSync in src/server.ts) with no path validation, so an attacker can write files outside the intended workspace.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Azure Data Explorer MCP Server: KQL Injection in multiple tools allows MCP client to execute arbitrary Kusto queries adx-mcp-server, at latest and commit 48b2933, contains KQL injection in three MCP tool handlers: get_table_schema, sample_table_data and get_table_details. The table_name parameter is interpolated into KQL via f-strings with no validation, so a caller or a prompt-injected agent can run arbitrary KQL against the Azure Data Explorer cluster, including reading other tables and issuing management commands such as.drop table. The flaw bypasses client trust boundaries because these tools are presented as safe metadata tools.
affected_vendors_raw: adx-mcp-server; Azure Data Explorer MCP Server

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n has XSS in Chat Trigger Node through Custom CSS An authenticated user with permission to create or modify workflows can inject JavaScript into the Custom CSS field of the n8n Chat Trigger node. A misconfiguration in the sanitize-html library lets the sanitization be bypassed, producing stored XSS on the public chat page that affects any user who visits the chat URL.
affected_vendors_raw: n8n; Chat Trigger Node; LangChain Chat Trigger node (@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.chatTrigger)

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: A weakness has been identified in huggingface smolagents 1.25.0.dev0. This affects the function… A weakness in huggingface smolagents 1.25.0.dev0, in the functions evaluate_augassign, evaluate_call and evaluate_with in src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py, allows code injection. It is an incomplete fix for VULNERABILITY_ID and can be triggered remotely. A public exploit exists, and the vendor did not respond to early disclosure.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI's Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) allows access to other users' memories VULNERABILITY_ID reports that Open WebUI v0.8.3 lets any authenticated user read other users' private files and memories through the POST /api/v1/retrieval/query/collection endpoint. The query_collection_handler in backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py checks authentication but performs no ownership validation on the supplied collection_names. The reporter also states that /api/v1/users/search exposes all user UUIDs, emails, names and roles, and that memory leakage requires the Memory experimental feature to be enabled.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI's process_files_batch() endpoint missing ownership check, allows unauthorized file overwrite Any authenticated Open WebUI user can overwrite any file by ID through the POST /api/v1/retrieval/process/files/batch endpoint, because process_files_batch() in backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py has no ownership check before writing. Attackers can obtain valid file UUIDs from GET /api/v1/knowledge/{id}/files for any knowledge base they can read, and the overwritten content is then served to the LLM via RAG. Tested on Open WebUI 0.8.3 in a default Docker configuration.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Open WebUI vulnerable to Path Traversal in `POST /api/v1/audio/transcriptions` An unsanitised filename field in the Open WebUI speech-to-text endpoint `POST /api/v1/audio/transcriptions` lets any authenticated non-admin user trigger a `FileNotFoundError`. The error message, including the server's absolute `DATA_DIR` path, is returned verbatim in the HTTP 400 response body. The source says this confirms information disclosure on all default deployments.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenHands is software for AI-driven development. Starting in version 1.5.0, a Command Injection vulnerability exists in… VULNERABILITY_ID affects OpenHands starting in version 1.5.0. The `path` parameter of the `/api/conversations/{conversation_id}/git/diff` endpoint is passed unsanitized to a shell command in `get_git_diff()` at `openhands/runtime/utils/git_handler.py:134`. An authenticated attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the agent sandbox, bypassing the normal channels through which the user may already instruct the agent to run commands.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs). Starting in version 0.10.1 and prior to… VULNERABILITY_ID affects vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models, from version 0.10.1 before 0.18.0. Two model implementation files hardcode `trust_remote_code=True` when loading sub-components, overriding a user's explicit `--trust-remote-code=False` opt-out. This enables remote code execution through malicious model repositories even when remote code trust is disabled.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw: Symlink Traversal via IDENTITY.md appendFile in agents.create/update (Incomplete Fix for VULNERABILITY_ID) The patch for VULNERABILITY_ID added symlink resolution and workspace boundary checks to agents.files.get and agents.files.set, but the agents.create and agents.update handlers in src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts still call fs.appendFile on IDENTITY.md with no symlink containment check. An attacker who can plant a symlink in the agent workspace can redirect that write to an arbitrary file, such as /etc/crontab, and inject agent name, emoji and avatar content into it.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PinchTab is a standalone HTTP server that gives AI agents direct control over a Chrome browser. PinchTab `v0.8.4`… PinchTab v0.8.4, a standalone HTTP server that gives AI agents control over Chrome, has a Windows-only command injection flaw in its orphaned Chrome cleanup path. The cleanup routine builds a PowerShell -Command string from a profile-derived needle, and the escaping only neutralizes backslashes, not other PowerShell metacharacters. An attacker with authenticated, administrative-equivalent access to instance lifecycle endpoints who launches an instance with a crafted profile name and triggers cleanup can run arbitrary PowerShell commands as the PinchTab OS user, not unauthenticated and without bypassing host privilege boundaries.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PinchTab is a standalone HTTP server that gives AI agents direct control over a Chrome browser. PinchTab `v0.7.7`… PinchTab v0.7.7 through v0.8.4 has incomplete request throttling on auth-checkable endpoints. In v0.7.7 through v0.8.3, RateLimitMiddleware in internal/handlers/middleware.go was never added to the production handler chain, and the pre-v0.8.4 limiter keyed clients by X-Forwarded-For, allowing header spoofing if enabled. v0.8.4 fixed both but still exempted /health and /metrics from rate limiting.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PinchTab is a standalone HTTP server that gives AI agents direct control over a Chrome browser. PinchTab `v0.7.8`… PinchTab, a standalone HTTP server giving AI agents direct control over a Chrome browser, versions v0.7.8 through v0.8.3 accepted the API token from a `token` URL query parameter as well as the `Authorization` header. A valid credential sent in the URL can be exposed through URIs recorded by reverse proxy access logs, browser and shell history, clipboard history, and tracing systems. The issue is an unsafe credential transport pattern rather than an authentication bypass, and it affects only deployments with a configured token where a client uses the query-parameter form.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PinchTab is a standalone HTTP server that gives AI agents direct control over a Chrome browser. PinchTab v0.8.3… PinchTab v0.8.3 contains a server-side request forgery issue in the optional scheduler's webhook delivery path. When a task submitted to POST /tasks has a user-controlled callbackUrl, the server sends an outbound POST to that URL without rejecting loopback or private destinations, and it follows redirects, enabling blind SSRF toward attacker-chosen targets reachable from the server. The scheduler is off by default, and in token-protected deployments the attacker must already hold the master API token.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw: Arbitrary code execution via unvalidated WebView JavascriptInterface OpenClaw's Android Canvas WebView accepted calls to its JavascriptInterface bridge from pages on untrusted origins, letting such pages inject instructions into the app. The affected npm package `openclaw` is any version below 2026.3.22, and the flaw is fixed in 2026.3.22 and later.

VULNERABILITY_ID: libcrux: Panic in Signature Hint Decoding During Verification The libcrux-ml-dsa library's hint decoding during ML-DSA signature verification did not check the boundedness of the cumulative hint counter for the last row of the hint vector. A manipulated invalid hint can cause an out-of-bounds memory access, because the decoding logic may read outside the bounds of the serialized signature, resulting in a runtime panic.

VULNERABILITY_ID: BentoML has Dockerfile Command Injection via system_packages in bentofile.yaml BentoML's docker.system_packages field in bentofile.yaml accepts arbitrary strings that are interpolated unescaped into Dockerfile RUN commands. A crafted bentofile.yaml therefore executes attacker-chosen shell commands during bentoml containerize or docker build, including in CI/CD pipelines and when BentoCloud builds user-supplied configs. The flaw affects all versions supporting that field, confirmed on 1.4.36.

VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n Has External Secrets Authorization Bypass in Credential Saving n8n has an authorization bypass in credential saving that affects instances with an external secrets vault configured. An authenticated user lacking the externalSecret:list permission can reference a secret by its external name in a credential and retrieve the plaintext value on save, bypassing that check. The attacker must know or guess the target secret's name.

VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n Has Authorization Bypass in OAuth Callback via N8N_SKIP_AUTH_ON_OAUTH_CALLBACK VULNERABILITY_ID affects n8n instances that explicitly set N8N_SKIP_AUTH_ON_OAUTH_CALLBACK to true. With that setting, the OAuth callback handler skips ownership verification of the OAuth state parameter, so an attacker can trick a victim into completing an OAuth flow against an attacker-controlled credential object. The victim's OAuth tokens are then stored in the attacker's credential, letting the attacker run workflows in the victim's name. The default configuration is not affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n is Vulnerable to Credential Theft via Name-Based Resolution and Permission Checker Bypass in Community Edition An authenticated user with the global:member role can chain flaws in n8n's credential pipeline to steal plaintext secrets from generic HTTP credentials (httpBasicAuth, httpHeaderAuth, httpQueryAuth) owned by other users on the same instance. A name-based resolution path that does not enforce ownership or project scope, combined with a permission checker bypass that skips generic HTTP credential types during pre-execution validation, lets the attacker run a workflow that decrypts and uses another user's credential. Native integration credential types and Enterprise Edition are not affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: @grackle-ai/powerline Runs Without Authentication by Default The PowerLine gRPC server in @grackle-ai/powerline runs with no authentication when neither the --token flag nor the GRACKLE_POWERLINE_TOKEN variable is set. It only logs a warning, and any client that can reach the port can spawn agent sessions, access credential tokens and execute code. The default binding to 127.0.0.1 limits exposure, but accidental network exposure, such as in a container or through port forwarding, makes the impact critical.

VULNERABILITY_ID: @grackle-ai/mcp has a workspace authorization bypass in its knowledge_search MCP tool The knowledge_search and knowledge_get_node MCP tools in @grackle-ai/mcp are listed in SCOPED_TOOLS, so scoped agents can call them, but their handlers do not receive authContext or enforce workspace scoping. A scoped agent in Workspace A can pass an arbitrary workspaceId to read knowledge graph data from Workspace B, bypassing workspace isolation (CWE-284).

VULNERABILITY_ID: @grackle-ai/server: Unescaped Error String in renderPairingPage() HTML Template VULNERABILITY_ID affects @grackle-ai/server. Its renderPairingPage() function interpolates the error parameter into HTML without escaping, unlike renderAuthorizePage() in the same file, which uses escapeHtml(). All current call sites pass hardcoded strings, so the flaw is not exploitable today, but a future change passing user-controlled content into that parameter would create an XSS vulnerability (CWE-79).

VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n has In-Process Memory Disclosure in its Task Runner An authenticated user with permission to create or modify workflows can use the JavaScript Task Runner in n8n to allocate uninitialized memory buffers. Those buffers may contain residual data from the same Node.js process, including prior requests, tasks, secrets, or tokens, when Task Runners are enabled with N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED=true. In external runner mode, exposure is limited to the external runner process.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Two LiteLLM versions published containing credential harvesting malware GitHub's Advisory Database published VULNERABILITY_ID on March 25, 2026, covering two malicious releases of the pip package litellm. Versions >= 1.82.7 and <= 1.82.8 were published containing credential harvesting malware, and the advisory lists no patched versions.

VULNERABILITY_ID: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server contains a vulnerability in the HTTP endpoint where an attacker may cause a denial of… VULNERABILITY_ID affects the HTTP endpoint of NVIDIA Triton Inference Server. An attacker can cause a denial of service by sending a large compressed payload, and a successful exploit may lead to denial of service. The weakness is classified as CWE-789, Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value.

VULNERABILITY_ID: NVIDIA Model Optimizer for Windows and Linux contains a vulnerability in the ONNX quantization feature, where a user… NVIDIA Model Optimizer for Windows and Linux contains a vulnerability in its ONNX quantization feature, classified as CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data). A user could trigger unsafe deserialization by supplying a specially crafted input file. Successful exploitation might lead to code execution, escalation of privileges, data tampering, and information disclosure.

VULNERABILITY_ID: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server contains a vulnerability where an attacker may cause internal state corruption. A… NVIDIA Triton Inference Server contains a vulnerability, VULNERABILITY_ID, where an attacker may cause internal state corruption. A successful exploit may lead to a denial of service. The weakness is classified as CWE-362, Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition').

VULNERABILITY_ID: NVIDIA APEX for Linux contains a vulnerability where an unauthorized attacker could cause a deserialization of… NVIDIA APEX for Linux contains a vulnerability, tracked as VULNERABILITY_ID and classified as CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data), that lets an unauthorized attacker cause deserialization of untrusted data. The flaw affects environments that use PyTorch versions earlier than 2.6. A successful exploit might lead to code execution, denial of service, escalation of privileges, data tampering, and information disclosure.

VULNERABILITY_ID: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server Sagemaker HTTP server contains a vulnerability where an attacker may cause an exception… NVIDIA Triton Inference Server's Sagemaker HTTP server contains a vulnerability, tracked as VULNERABILITY_ID, that lets an attacker cause an exception. A successful exploit may lead to denial of service. The weakness is classified as CWE-362, a race condition from concurrent execution using a shared resource with improper synchronization. NVD has not yet provided an assessment.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow is a tool for building and deploying AI-powered agents and workflows. An unauthenticated remote shell… Multiple GitHub Actions workflows in the Langflow repository prior to version 1.9.0 interpolate GitHub context variables such as `${{ github.head_ref }}` directly into `run:` steps without sanitization. A malicious branch name or pull request title lets an unauthenticated attacker inject and execute arbitrary shell commands during CI/CD runs, potentially exposing secrets such as `GITHUB_TOKEN`, manipulating infrastructure, or compromising the supply chain. The proof of concept sends the CI token to an external URL.

VULNERABILITY_ID: New API is a large language mode (LLM) gateway and artificial intelligence (AI) asset management system. Prior to… New API, an LLM gateway and AI asset management system, is vulnerable before version 0.11.4-alpha.2. An Insecure Direct Object Reference in the GET /v1/videos/:task_id/content endpoint lets any authenticated user access other users' video content. The server also authenticates to upstream providers (Google Gemini, OpenAI) using credentials derived from tasks the attacker does not own. The cause is that model.GetByOnlyTaskId(taskID) queries by task_id alone, without a user_id filter.

VULNERABILITY_ID: A vulnerability was identified in PyTorch 2.10.0. The affected element is an unknown function of the component pt2… VULNERABILITY_ID affects PyTorch 2.10.0, specifically an unknown function in the pt2 Loading Handler component. Manipulation of this component leads to deserialization, and the attack can only be performed from a local environment. A public exploit is available, and the project was informed early through a pull request but has not responded; NVD has not yet provided an assessment,

VULNERABILITY_ID: A security flaw has been discovered in apconw Aix-DB up to 1.2.3. This impacts an unknown function of the file… VULNERABILITY_ID is a flaw in apconw Aix-DB up to 1.2.3, in an unknown function of agent/text2sql/rag/terminology_retriever.py. Manipulating the Description argument leads to SQL injection, and the attack requires local access. A public exploit has been released, and the vendor did not respond to early disclosure.

VULNERABILITY_ID: langflow: /profile_pictures/{folder_name}/{file_name} endpoint file reading VULNERABILITY_ID affects langflow. The download_profile_picture function behind the /profile_pictures/{folder_name}/{file_name} endpoint in src/backend/base/langflow/api/v1/files.py does not strictly filter the folder_name and file_name parameters, so a request can traverse directories and read the secret_key. An attacker who obtains the secret_key can forge JWT authentication tokens and log into the system.

VULNERABILITY_ID: langflow has Unauthenticated IDOR on Image Downloads The `/api/v1/files/images/{flow_id}/{file_name}` endpoint in langflow serves image files without authentication or an ownership check. Any unauthenticated request that includes a known `flow_id` and `file_name` returns the image with HTTP 200. In multi-tenant deployments, an attacker who can obtain a flow UUID, which other API responses may leak, can download any user's uploaded images without credentials.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PinchTab is a standalone HTTP server that gives AI agents direct control over a Chrome browser. Versions 0.8.2 and… PinchTab, a standalone HTTP server giving AI agents control of a Chrome browser, versions 0.8.2 and below, has a blind SSRF flaw in its /download endpoint. validateDownloadURL() checks only the initial user-supplied URL, so the embedded Chromium browser can follow attacker-controlled redirects or navigations to internal network addresses after validation. Exploitation requires security.allowDownload=true, which is disabled by default.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Server-side request forgery (ssrf) in Microsoft 365 Copilot's Business Chat allows an authorized attacker to elevate… VULNERABILITY_ID is a server-side request forgery (CWE-918) in Microsoft 365 Copilot's Business Chat. According to the description, an authorized attacker over a network can use it to elevate privileges. NVD has not yet provided an assessment, and the record was published on 03/19/2026.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Microsoft Copilot allows an… VULNERABILITY_ID is a command injection weakness (CWE-77) in Microsoft Copilot, reported by Microsoft Corporation. The source describes it as an improper neutralization of special elements used in a command, which allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. The NVD has not yet provided an assessment, and the record was published and last modified on 03/19/2026.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in M365 Copilot allows an… VULNERABILITY_ID is an improper neutralization of special elements used in a command (CWE-77, command injection) in M365 Copilot. An unauthorized attacker can exploit it over a network to disclose information. NIST has not yet provided an NVD assessment, and Microsoft Corporation is the listed source.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow has an Arbitrary File Write (RCE) via v2 API VULNERABILITY_ID reports an Arbitrary File Write in Langflow via the POST /api/v2/files/ endpoint. The multipart upload filename is passed unchecked to LocalStorageService, which lacks a containment check, so an authenticated attacker can write files anywhere on the host, potentially leading to Remote Code Execution. The reporter tested this against langflowai/langflow:latest (v1.7.3).

VULNERABILITY_ID: Cross-Site Tool Execution for HTTP Servers without Authorizatrion in github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk The Go SDK for MCP (github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk) had a flaw in its Streamable HTTP transport. It accepted browser-generated cross-site POST requests without validating the Origin header or requiring Content-Type: application/json. Without Authorization configured, especially in stateless or sessionless setups, any website could send MCP requests to a local server and potentially trigger tool execution. Cross-site POSTs with Content-Type: text/plain could reach message handling without a CORS preflight barrier.
affected_vendors_raw: MCP Go SDK; Model Context Protocol

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: Improper handling of null Unicode character when parsing JSON in github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk The Go SDK for the Model Context Protocol moved to the segmentio/encoding library for JSON parsing in version 1.3.1. The new parser matched keys that had null Unicode characters appended to their base names, so combined with duplicate keys, a "last key wins" resolution could override the intended MCP message. This could let messages evade proxies or policy layers that match exact field names, and other MCP SDKs in TypeScript and Python would reject the same messages.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Claude Code has a Workspace Trust Dialog Bypass via Repo-Controlled Settings File Claude Code resolved its permission mode from settings files, including the repo-controlled `.claude/settings.json`, before showing the workspace trust confirmation dialog. A malicious repository could set `permissions.defaultMode` to `bypassPermissions` in that committed file, so the dialog was silently skipped on first open and the user was placed in a permissive mode. This made it easier for an attacker-controlled repository to gain tool execution without explicit user consent.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Mesop Affected by Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Test Suite Route /exec-py The Mesop test sandbox server, in ai/sandbox/wsgi_app.py, exposes a /exec-py route that accepts a base64-encoded Python string in the code form parameter, writes it to disk and runs it with execute_module(module_path...). The route performs no authentication, so any client that can reach it can run arbitrary commands on the host. The impact is most relevant to publicly exposed or unfirewalled deployments.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Mesop has a Path Traversal utilizing `FileStateSessionBackend` leads to Application Denial of Service and File Write/Deletion VULNERABILITY_ID is a path traversal flaw in Mesop when it uses the disk-based `FileStateSessionBackend`. The `state_token` field of a `UserEvent` sent to the `ui_stream` endpoint in `mesop/server/server.py` is passed unchecked to `_make_file_path`, so `../` sequences can point file access outside `base_dir`. The source states this can cause denial of service through crash loops and arbitrary file reads, writes or deletions.

VULNERABILITY_ID: SSRF in @aborruso/ckan-mcp-server via base_url allows access to internal networks The @aborruso/ckan-mcp-server MCP server accepts a base_url parameter in tools such as ckan_package_search and sparql_query and sends HTTP requests to it without restriction. Exploitation needs prompt injection through malicious content while the assistant has this server connected, and a proof of concept sent 9 requests to a canary endpoint. An attacker could scan internal networks, steal cloud metadata credentials via 169.254.169.254, and attempt SQL or SPARQL injection.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow is Missing Ownership Verification in API Key Deletion (IDOR) Langflow's DELETE endpoint for API keys, delete_api_key_route() in src/backend/base/langflow/api/v1/api_key.py, checks only that the caller is authenticated. The delete_api_key() CRUD function in crud.py does not verify that the key belongs to the current user, so any authenticated user can delete other users' API keys by ID. The source says this enables account takeover, denial of service, and disruption of other users' integrations.

VULNERABILITY_ID: AWS API MCP File Access Restriction Bypass The AWS API MCP Server, an open source Model Context Protocol server that lets AI assistants run AWS CLI commands, contains an Improper Protection of Alternate Path flaw in its no-access and workdir file access features. Versions >= 0.2.14 and < 1.3.9, on all platforms, can bypass the intended file restriction and expose arbitrary local file contents in the MCP client application context.
affected_vendors_raw: AWS API MCP Server; Model Context Protocol (MCP); AWS CLI

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Langflow via Public Flow Build Endpoint The POST /api/v1/build_public_tmp/{flow_id}/flow endpoint in Langflow builds public flows without authentication. When the optional data parameter is supplied, the endpoint uses attacker-controlled flow data instead of the stored flow, and node definitions containing arbitrary Python code reach exec() in prepare_global_scope (src/lfx/src/lfx/custom/validate.py) with no sandboxing. The source states that the SHA256 check validates against a manifest that the attacker controls, so a malicious model can carry a matching hash. The source says that when chained with file-system vulnerabilities, a model loaded this way can silently exfiltrate files such as SSH keys and cloud credentials.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastMCP OAuth Proxy token reuse across MCP servers The FastMCP OAuth Proxy ignores the client-supplied `resource` parameter in authorization and token requests and issues tokens for the `base_url` set at initialization instead. Because the tokens carry no resource information, a benign MCP server cannot verify that a token was issued for it. An attacker can run a malicious MCP server that advertises the benign proxy as its authorization server, capture the token from a victim's OAuth flow, and replay it against other MCP servers that share that authorization server.

VULNERABILITY_ID: AI command injection in M365 Copilot allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. VULNERABILITY_ID describes an AI command injection flaw in M365 Copilot. The source states that an unauthorized attacker can exploit it over a network to disclose information. NVD has not yet provided an assessment, and the vulnerability was published on 03/16/2026.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is a ChatGPT clone with additional features. Prior to 0.8.3-rc1, a Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability… VULNERABILITY_ID affects LibreChat versions prior to 0.8.3-rc1. VULNERABILITY_ID: LibreChat is a ChatGPT clone with additional features. model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: ha-mcp has XSS via Unescaped HTML in OAuth Consent Form The ha-mcp OAuth consent form renders user-controlled parameters through Python f-strings without HTML escaping, so an attacker who registers a client with a malicious client_name via the /register endpoint can run JavaScript in the server operator's browser after that operator follows a crafted authorization URL. Successful exploitation could exfiltrate data entered into the consent form, including the Home Assistant Long-Lived Access Token.

VULNERABILITY_ID: FastGPT is an AI Agent building platform. In 4.14.7 and earlier, FastGPT's Python Sandbox (fastgpt-sandbox) includes… VULNERABILITY_ID affects FastGPT, an AI Agent building platform, in version 4.14.7 and earlier. Its Python Sandbox (fastgpt-sandbox) relies on static detection and seccomp to block file writes, but an attacker can remap stdout (fd 1) to an arbitrary writable file descriptor using fcntl. Because sys.stdout.write() still satisfies the seccomp rule write(fd==1), the attacker can create or overwrite arbitrary files inside the sandbox container.

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise is a drag & drop user interface to build a customized large language model flow. Prior to 3.0.13, Flowise… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Flowise before 3.0.13. Its HTTP Node in AgentFlow and Chatflow makes server-side HTTP requests to user-controlled URLs, with no default restrictions on private or internal IP ranges (RFC 1918), localhost, or cloud metadata endpoints. Any user interacting with a publicly exposed chatflow can thus force the server to reach internal network resources.

VULNERABILITY_ID: MCP Atlassian has an arbitrary file write leading to arbitrary code execution via unconstrained download_path in confluence_download_attachment VULNERABILITY_ID affects MCP Atlassian. The confluence_download_attachment tool accepts a download_path parameter that is written to without any directory boundary enforcement, so an attacker who controls an attachment's content can write it to any path the server process can write, such as /etc/cron.d/, leading to arbitrary code execution. The MCP HTTP transport carries no authentication by default and binds to 0.0.0.0, so the issue is reachable from the local network.

VULNERABILITY_ID: MCP Atlassian has SSRF via unvalidated X-Atlassian-Jira-Url / X-Atlassian-Confluence-Url headers mcp-atlassian's HTTP middleware and dependency layer accept an unvalidated X-Atlassian-Jira-Url (and the Confluence equivalent) from unauthenticated requests when no Authorization header is present. The server then issues an outbound GET to {header_url}/rest/api/2/myself, enabling server-side request forgery, which the advisory says can expose IAM credentials via 169.254.169.254 in cloud deployments and enable internal network reconnaissance and injection of attacker-controlled content into LLM tool results.

VULNERABILITY_ID: vLLM has SSRF Protection Bypass The SSRF protection fix in vLLM's `load_from_url_async` method, in `vllm/connections.py`, can be bypassed. The fix validates URLs with `urllib3.util.parse_url()`, but the actual requests use `aiohttp`, which relies on the `yarl` library. The two parsers handle backslash characters differently. A URL such as `https://httpbin.org\@evil.com/` passes validation with host `httpbin.org` but is requested from `evil.com`, which lets an attacker bypass the hostname allowlist and reach arbitrary internal or external services.

VULNERABILITY_ID: PinchTab is a standalone HTTP server that gives AI agents direct control over a Chrome browser. Prior to version 0.7.7… PinchTab, a standalone HTTP server that gives AI agents direct control over a Chrome browser, contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) flaw in its /download endpoint in versions prior to 0.7.7 (CWE-918). Any user with API access can make the server request arbitrary URLs, including internal network services and local system files, and exfiltrate the full response content.

VULNERABILITY_ID: WeKnora Vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via SQL Injection Bypass in AI Database Query Tool A remote code execution flaw in WeKnora's database query tool lets an unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary code on the database server with database user privileges. The Phase 5 validateNode() function in internal/utils/inject.go has no handler for ArrayExpr or RowExpr nodes, so dangerous PostgreSQL functions such as pg_read_file() nested inside array expressions skip validation and pass all seven checks.

VULNERABILITY_ID: WeKnora has Broken Access Control - Cross-Tenant Data Exposure WeKnora's database query tool fails to enforce tenant isolation on the models, messages and embeddings tables, which are allowed by WithSecurityDefaults() but absent from the tenantID-filtered list in internal/utils/inject.go. Any authenticated tenant can run SELECT queries against these tables and read other tenants' data, including API keys, model configurations and private messages, with no extra precondition beyond ordinary user access.

VULNERABILITY_ID: WeKnora Vulnerable to Tool Execution Hijacking via Ambigous Naming Convention In MCP client and Indirect Prompt Injection WeKnora's MCP client builds internal tool names as `mcp_{service}_{tool}` after sanitizing each part, and its registry (`internal/agent/tools/registry.go`) silently overwrites existing entries. A malicious remote MCP server can register a tool such as `tavily_extract` that replaces the legitimate one, and the client also feeds MCP tool descriptions and results into the LLM context without sanitization. The source states that this lets an attacker redirect LLM execution, exfiltrate system prompts and context, and potentially run other tools with the user's privileges, with a precondition that the user registers the malicious service before the legitimate one.

VULNERABILITY_ID: WeKnora Vulnerable to Broken Access Control in Tenant Management WeKnora's tenant management endpoints (GET /api/v1/tenants, GET, PUT and DELETE /api/v1/tenants/{id}) do not check that the caller owns the tenant or holds cross-tenant privileges. Any authenticated user can therefore read, modify or delete any tenant by ID, and because account registration is open, an unauthenticated attacker can register and exploit this. The reporter demonstrates that listing tenants exposes other tenants' API keys, which grant actions on those accounts.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise Missing Authentication on NVIDIA NIM Endpoints Flowise's global authentication middleware whitelists the `/api/v1/nvidia-nim` route through `WHITELIST_URLS` in `packages/server/src/utils/constants.ts`, so no JWT or API-key check runs for any endpoint under `/api/v1/nvidia-nim/*`, and the controllers in `packages/server/src/controllers/nvidia-nim/index.ts` perform no authentication of their own. Unauthenticated callers can reach `/get-token`, which returns a valid NVIDIA API token, and endpoints that list, start, stop and pull Docker containers and images. The issue is rated under CWE-306.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise has IDOR leading to Account Takeover and Enterprise Feature Bypass via SSO Configuration VULNERABILITY_ID describes an Insecure Direct Object Reference in the PUT /api/v1/loginmethod endpoint of the Flowise platform. The endpoint accepts an organizationId from the JSON body and updates that organization's record without checking that the authenticated user owns it or has admin rights, so any low-privileged user, including Free plan users, can overwrite another organization's SSO configuration. The source states this enables Account Takeover by replacing the victim's OAuth credentials with attacker-controlled ones, and enabling Enterprise-only SSO features without a license.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise Allows Mass Assignment in `/api/v1/leads` Endpoint A mass assignment flaw in the `/api/v1/leads` endpoint of Flowise lets unauthenticated users set internal entity fields (`id`, `createdDate`, `chatId`) by including them in the request body. The `createLead` function in `/packages/server/src/services/leads/index.ts` calls `Object.assign(newLead, body)` without filtering fields, overwriting the auto-generated values before save. The endpoint is listed in `WHITELIST_URLS` in `/packages/server/src/utils/constants.ts`, so no authentication is required. The source is tagged CWE-915.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Agentgateway is an open source data plane for agentic AI connectivity within or across any agent framework or… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Agentgateway, an open source data plane for agentic AI connectivity, prior to version 0.12.0. When converting an MCP tools/call request to an OpenAPI request, input path, query, and header values are not sanitized, which is classified as CWE-20 Improper Input Validation. The NVD assessment has not yet been provided.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise has Arbitrary File Upload via MIME Spoofing The `/api/v1/attachments/:chatflowId/:chatId` endpoint in Flowise is listed in `WHITELIST_URLS`, so it accepts uploads without authentication. The server checks uploads against the MIME types in `chatbotConfig.fullFileUpload.allowedUploadFileTypes` but trusts the client-supplied `Content-Type` header without checking file contents or extension. An attacker can upload scripts or other arbitrary files by declaring a permitted type such as `application/pdf`, and the files persist in backend storage. Chained with static hosting or file retrieval, this can lead to Stored XSS, malicious file hosting, or Remote Code Execution.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise has Authorization Bypass via Spoofed x-request-from Header Flowise trusts any HTTP client that sends the header `x-request-from: internal`, so an authenticated tenant session with only a browser cookie can bypass the authorization checks on `/api/v1/**`. The flaw sits in the global middleware at `external/Flowise/packages/server/src/index.ts:214`, which calls `verifyToken` for that header and runs no further permission checks. The source says the bypass grants access to internal administration endpoints such as `/api/v1/apikey`, `/api/v1/credentials`, `/api/v1/tools` and `/api/v1/node-custom-function`, and that all self-hosted Flowise 3.0.8 deployments using the default middleware are affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: GitHub Copilot CLI Dangerous Shell Expansion Patterns Enable Arbitrary Code Execution GitHub Copilot CLI's shell tool contains a vulnerability in which crafted bash parameter expansion patterns (such as ${var@P}, assignment forms like ${var=value}, indirect ${!var}, and nested $(cmd) inside ${...}) can hide command execution inside commands the safety assessment classifies as read-only. An attacker who can influence the commands the agent runs, for example through prompt injection in repository files, MCP server responses, or user instructions, could achieve arbitrary code execution on the user's workstation, even in modes that require approval for write operations. The issue affects versions prior to 0.0.423.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenSift is an AI study tool that sifts through large datasets using semantic search and generative AI. Prior to… VULNERABILITY_ID affects OpenSift, an AI study tool that uses semantic search and generative AI, in versions prior to 1.6.3-alpha. Its URL ingest pipeline accepted user-controlled remote URLs with incomplete destination restrictions, so private and local host checks were missing coverage for credentialed URLs, non-standard ports, and cross-host redirects, leaving SSRF-class abuse paths in non-localhost deployments. The issue is classified as CWE-918.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenSift is an AI study tool that sifts through large datasets using semantic search and generative AI. VULNERABILITY_ID: The Greenshift – animation and page builder blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure… VULNERABILITY_ID affects the Greenshift – animation and page builder blocks plugin for WordPress in all versions up to and including 12.8.3. The plugin stores an automated Settings Backup in a publicly accessible file, so unauthenticated attackers can extract the configured OpenAI, Claude, Google Maps, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Cloudflare Turnstile API keys. model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw versions prior to 2026.2.14 contain server-side request forgery vulnerabilities in the Feishu extension that… VULNERABILITY_ID affects OpenClaw versions prior to 2026.2.14 in the Feishu extension. VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise Vulnerable to PII Disclosure on Unauthenticated Forgot Password Endpoint Flowise's POST /api/v1/account/forgot-password endpoint returns the full user object, including id, name, email, status and timestamps, instead of a generic acknowledgment. VULNERABILITY_ID: Flowise has Insufficient Password Salt Rounds Flowise's getHash function in packages/server/src/enterprise/utils/encryption.util.ts uses a default bcrypt salt round count of 5, set through the PASSWORD_SALT_HASH_ROUNDS environment variable, which yields 2^5 = 32 iterations. The source states this is below the OWASP recommendation of 10 rounds (1024 iterations), so stored password hashes are easier to brute-force if the database is compromised. The same default is used in resetPassword (account.service.ts:568). Tracked as CWE-916 with.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LangGraph checkpoint loading has unsafe msgpack deserialization LangGraph checkpointers can load msgpack-encoded checkpoints that reconstruct Python objects during deserialization. An attacker who can write attacker-controlled checkpoint bytes to the backing store, for example after a database compromise, may supply a crafted payload that triggers unsafe object reconstruction when the checkpoint is loaded, potentially leading to code execution in the application runtime. The source states there is no evidence of exploitation in the wild.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Fickling missing RCE-capable modules in UNSAFE_IMPORTS fickling versions up to and including 0.1.8 have an incomplete UNSAFE_IMPORTS blocklist that omits the stdlib modules uuid, _osx_support and _aix_support. Functions in these modules, such as uuid._get_command_stdout, _aix_support._read_cmd_output and _osx_support._find_build_tool, call subprocess.Popen() or os.system() with attacker-controlled arguments. A malicious pickle importing them passes fickling's UnsafeImports and NonStandardImports checks, and pickle.loads() runs the command.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw Canvas Authentication Bypass Vulnerability OpenClaw's gateway function `authorizeCanvasRequest()` in `src/gateway/server-http.ts` grants canvas endpoints (`/__openclaw__/a2ui/`, `/__openclaw__/canvas/`, `/__openclaw__/ws`) access to any HTTP request from a private IP that matches an authenticated WebSocket client, without checking the request's own credentials. Tested on openclaw 2026.2.17 on macOS 26.3, the flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker sharing an IP with a legitimate client, such as behind corporate NAT or in Kubernetes or Docker shared networking, gain full canvas access.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw has agent avatar symlink traversal in gateway session metadata A crafted local avatar path in OpenClaw's gateway can follow a symlink outside the agent workspace and return arbitrary file contents as a base64 data: URL. The flaw sits in resolveIdentityAvatarUrl in src/gateway/session-utils.ts, affects the openclaw npm package from v2026.1.21 through 2026.2.21-2, and allows local file read in the gateway process, which agents.list can return as avatarUrl.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw: Slack interactive callbacks could skip configured sender checks in some shared-workspace flows OpenClaw versions `<= 2026.2.24` accepted some Slack interactive callbacks (`block_action`, `view_submission`, `view_closed`) before full sender authorization checks in shared workspace deployments that use sender restrictions. An unauthorized workspace member could enqueue system-event text into an active session, but the issue did not by itself provide unauthenticated access, cross-gateway isolation bypass, or host-level privilege escalation.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw reuses the gateway auth token in the owner ID prompt hashing fallback OpenClaw, the npm package `openclaw`, reused `gateway.auth.token` and `gateway.remote.token` as a fallback secret for hashing owner IDs in prompts when `commands.ownerDisplay=hash` is set and `commands.ownerDisplaySecret` is unset. This linked gateway authentication to prompt metadata hashing, and the hash outputs are visible to third-party model providers in system prompts, though no plaintext token is disclosed directly. Risk is highest when operators use weak gateway tokens and leave the owner hash secret unset. Versions up to and including 2026.2.21-2 are affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw hook transform path containment missed symlink-resolved escapes The openclaw npm package, versions up to and including 2026.2.21-2, validated webhook transform modules with lexical path checks only. A symlink under the hooks transform tree could resolve outside the trusted directory and be dynamically imported, so the gateway may run unintended JavaScript with gateway-process privileges. Exploitation requires enabled, reachable hook transforms and an attacker able to influence transform path resolution.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw vulnerable to arbitrary file read via $include directive A path traversal flaw (CWE-22) in OpenClaw's config `$include` resolution lets anyone who can modify the config read arbitrary local files outside the config directory. Absolute paths, `../` traversal and symlinks inside the config directory all reach external files unless real-path checks are enforced. Exposure is bounded by the OpenClaw runtime user's file permissions, and the impact includes local API keys and private config material.

VULNERABILITY_ID: BentoML Vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Symlink Path Traversal in Tar Extraction BentoML's `safe_extract_tarfile()` in `src/bentoml/_internal/utils/filesystem.py` checks only a tar member's own path, not the target of a symlink member. A crafted bento or model tar can therefore place a symlink pointing outside the extraction directory and then write a regular file through it, giving arbitrary file write on the host. The source says all versions containing `safe_extract_tarfile()` are affected.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw: macOS beta onboarding exposed PKCE verifier via OAuth state OpenClaw's macOS app onboarding flow, which is still in beta, used the PKCE code_verifier as the OAuth state value during Anthropic OAuth sign-in, exposing that secret in front-channel URL state. Affected versions are openclaw (npm) up to and including 2026.2.24; core CLI and gateway onboarding paths are not affected. Exploitation required obtaining both the OAuth authorization artifacts and the exposed state values during that flow.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw has hook auth rate limiter bypass via IPv4-mapped IPv6 client key variants OpenClaw's hook authentication throttle keyed failed attempts by raw socket remoteAddress text, so IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms of the same client (such as 1.2.3.4 and::ffff:1.2.3.4) received separate rate-limit buckets. An attacker could split failed attempts across both forms and double the brute-force budget from 20 to 40 attempts per 60-second window. Affected are the openclaw npm package at versions <= 2026.2.21-2, in src/gateway/server-http.ts and src/gateway/auth-rate-limit.ts.

VULNERABILITY_ID: The AI ChatBot with ChatGPT and Content Generator by AYS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized access and… VULNERABILITY_ID affects the AI ChatBot with ChatGPT and Content Generator by AYS plugin for WordPress, in all versions up to and including 2.7.5. Missing capability checks on the store_data() and get_chatgpt_api_key() functions let unauthenticated attackers view, modify or delete the plugin's ChatGPT API key. The weakness is classified as CWE-862, Missing Authorization.

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenClaw: Gateway /tools/invoke tool escalation + ACP permission auto-approval OpenClaw Gateway's authenticated POST /tools/invoke endpoint did not deny high-risk session orchestration tools such as sessions_spawn and sessions_send by default, so a caller holding a valid Gateway token could create or control agent sessions and inject messages across sessions. ACP clients could also auto-approve permission requests for risky tools with insufficient user interaction. The advisory affects openclaw versions before 2026.2.14.

An authenticated attacker, including a prompt-injected AI agent holding the gateway token, can read arbitrary files such as /etc/passwd, and the contents are forwarded to a connected node via canvas.a2ui.pushJSONL. Tested on openclaw 2026.2.17 and macOS 26.3.

VULNERABILITY_ID: OpenChatBI has a Path Traversal Vulnerability in save_report Tool OpenChatBI versions up to and including 0.2.1 have a path traversal flaw in the save_report tool in openchatbi/tool/save_report.py. The file_format parameter is only stripped of leading dots, so sequences like /../../ survive and are concatenated into the output filename, letting an attacker manipulated through the LLM write files outside the report directory, such as overwriting __init__.py, potentially leading to remote code execution.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Gradio is an open-source Python package designed for quick prototyping. Prior to version 6.6.0, a Server-Side Request… VULNERABILITY_ID is an SSRF flaw in Gradio, an open-source Python package for quick prototyping, in versions prior to 6.6.0. When a victim application calls `gr.load()` on an attacker-controlled Space, the malicious `proxy_url` from the config is trusted and added to the allowlist. An attacker can then make arbitrary HTTP requests from the victim's server, reaching internal services, cloud metadata endpoints and private networks.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Gradio is an open-source Python package designed for quick prototyping. VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n has a Guardrail Node Bypass VULNERABILITY_ID describes a bypass of the default guardrail instructions in n8n's Guardrail node. An end user interacting with a workflow that uses the node could craft an input that gets past those instructions.

VULNERABILITY_ID: n8n has an Authentication Bypass in its Chat Trigger Node The Chat Trigger node in n8n can be configured with n8n User Auth, a non-default authentication method. When that configuration is used, the authentication check can be circumvented. The issue requires this non-default configuration to be in place.

VULNERABILITY_ID: MCP Go SDK Vulnerable to Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity The Go MCP SDK parsed JSON-RPC and MCP messages with Go's standard encoding/json.Unmarshal, which matches keys case-insensitively and folds Unicode characters such as ſ (U+017F) and K (U+212A) to ASCII. A malicious MCP peer could send non-standard field casing, such as "Method" instead of "method", that the SDK silently accepted. This could let such messages bypass intermediary proxies or policy layers that match exact field names, and it made the Go SDK inconsistent with the case-sensitive TypeScript and Python SDKs.

model_text: VULNERABILITY_ID: Deserialization of untrusted data in the LanguageModel class of Flair from versions 0.4.1 to latest are vulnerable to… VULNERABILITY_ID affects the LanguageModel class of Flair, from version 0.4.1 to the latest release. Deserialization of untrusted data in this class allows arbitrary code execution when a malicious model is loaded. The weakness is classified as CWE-502, and NVD has not yet provided an assessment.

VULNERABILITY_ID: Langflow is a tool for building and deploying AI-powered agents and workflows. Prior to version 1.8.0, the CSV Agent… VULNERABILITY_ID affects Langflow versions prior to 1.8.0. An attacker can use prompt injection to execute arbitrary Python and OS commands on the server, resulting in full Remote Code Execution (RCE). The weakness is classified as CWE-94.

VULNERABILITY_ID: LangGraph: BaseCache Deserialization of Untrusted Data may lead to Remote Code Execution LangGraph's caching layer can deserialize attacker-controlled cache entries with pickle.loads when msgpack serialization fails.
